This enables the same physical laboratory to support remote interactive use, scripted experiments, autonomous routines, and features such as version control. We implement PICO on a robotic free-space optics platform and demonstrate it through an experimental case study.
tldr: The paper presents PICO, a robotic cloud-laboratory architecture that provides a domain-specific software abstraction layer for programming, operating, and reproducing reconfigurable free-space optical experiments remotely.
motivation: Laboratory automation can improve experimental throughput, accessibility, and reproducibility, but existing robotic lab systems are hard to reconfigure, especially in free-space optics where heterogeneous components demand precise alignment and frequent rearrangement.
method: The authors design a common domain-specific abstraction and software layer that maps experimental configurations and actions across multiple user interfaces, and implement it on a robotic free-space optics platform supporting remote interactive use, scripted experiments, autonomous routines, and version control.
result: PICO is demonstrated on a robotic free-space optics platform through an experimental case study, showing that the same physical laboratory can serve remote, scripted, and autonomous workflows.
conclusion: Programmable cloud-laboratory infrastructure can make reconfigurable optical experiments easier to program, operate, and reproduce, though the work is a systems/automation contribution rather than a quantum information or thermodynamics result.

title: Exact Ionization Amplitudes For A Delta-Function Well In An Arbitrary-Strength Dc Electric Field
authors: Gerald J. Iafrate Ilki Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate finite-time field-induced ionization from a one-dimensional attractive delta-function well in a uniform dc electric field of arbitrary strength. Our aim is to determine the physical bound-state survival amplitude \(a_b(t)\) at any observation time without constructing the complete time-dependent propagator or wavefunction. In the gauge-equivalent Kramers--Henneberger representation, the field appears as motion of the contact point, and the resulting dynamics reduces to a closed Volterra equation. Exact endpoint-phase factorization organizes the full chronological rescattering history into a relative-time convolution hierarchy and an exact resolvent. By introducing the accumulated bound-state amplitude and reorganizing its two-time domain in relative and complementary center times, the final contact contribution becomes an explicit boundary integral. All spatial integrations are carried out analytically. The field-driven contact-free term is obtained in closed form using the Faddeeva function, while the direct and repeated-rescattering terms are expressed as explicitly evaluable time integrals. The result applies at arbitrary dc-field strength and finite time, with no weak-field expansion, rescattering truncation, or asymptotic-time approximation. It is verified through the exact field-free limit and an independent numerical solution of the original physical Volterra equation. The formulation gives an exact nonperturbative solution of a fundamental ionization model and reveals otherwise hidden analytical structure in driven quantum dynamics.
tldr: The paper derives exact finite-time ionization amplitudes for a one-dimensional delta-function well in an arbitrary-strength dc electric field using the Kramers-Henneberger representation and a closed Volterra equation.
motivation: Strong-field ionization is a fundamental nonperturbative process, but exact finite-time solutions for simple model systems are rare and can reveal analytical structure hidden in driven quantum dynamics.
method: The authors transform to the gauge-equivalent Kramers-Henneberger frame, reduce the dynamics to a Volterra equation, and use endpoint-phase factorization to organize rescattering contributions; spatial integrations are done analytically, yielding closed-form terms involving the Faddeeva function.
result: They obtain the bound-state survival amplitude exactly at arbitrary dc-field strength and finite time, verified against the field-free limit and an independent numerical solution of the original Volterra equation.
conclusion: The work provides an exact nonperturbative solution of a fundamental ionization model and exposes hidden analytical structure in field-driven quantum dynamics.

title: A Proof Of The Fong--Tsui Conjecture
authors: Mohamed Amine Aouichaoui, Fuad Kittaneh, Yicen Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a bounded operator [MATH] on a complex Hilbert space is self-adjoint whenever [MATH], as conjectured by Fong and Tsui .
tldr: The paper proves the Fong–Tsui conjecture that a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space is self-adjoint under a specified condition.
motivation: The Fong–Tsui conjecture proposed a criterion for self-adjointness of bounded Hilbert-space operators, and this work aims to resolve it.
method: The authors provide an operator-theoretic proof establishing the conjectured self-adjointness condition for bounded operators on complex Hilbert spaces.
result: The conjecture is proven: whenever the given condition holds, the bounded operator is necessarily self-adjoint.
conclusion: This resolves the Fong–Tsui conjecture and contributes a result to operator theory on Hilbert spaces.

title: Structure-Driven Inversion: A New Paradigm For Solving Inverse Problems
authors: Shengchang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverse problems are predominantly solved within the optimization-driven paradigm, which formulates the problem as objective-function minimization and approaches the solution by iterative search. Though universal, it suffers from limitations in efficiency, interpretability, and multi-parameter decoupling. This paper proposes a new paradigm---Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI). Instead of iterative search, SDI identifies and exploits the intrinsic structure of the problem to construct a solution method. It has two types of structure---mathematical structure and physical structure---and two corresponding driving inversion types: Mathematical Structure-Driven Inversion (MSDI) and Physical Structure-Driven Inversion (PSDI). The current representative method of MSDI is Mathematical Structure-Driven Pseudo-Inverse Inversion (MSDPII), which constructs a pseudo-inverse in the spectral domain via unitary diagonalization. The current representative methods of PSDI are Physical Structure-Driven Waveform Inversion Imaging (PSDWII), which performs inversion through virtual-source projection, and Physical Structure-Driven Back-Propagation (PSDBP), which implements three structural projections for deep neural networks via physical-system analogy. SDI is not a rejection but a complement and extension of Optimization-Driven Inversion (ODI). To the best of the author's knowledge, no existing study has systematically presented structure-driven inversion as an independent paradigm; this paper aims to fill that gap.
tldr: The paper proposes a new structure-driven inversion (SDI) paradigm for solving inverse problems by exploiting mathematical or physical structure rather than iterative optimization.
motivation: Existing optimization-driven inversion suffers from inefficiency, poor interpretability, and difficulty in decoupling multiple parameters, motivating a structure-based alternative.
method: SDI uses mathematical structure (e.g., spectral-domain pseudo-inverse via unitary diagonalization) or physical structure (e.g., virtual-source projection, back-propagation with structural projections for deep neural networks) to construct inversion solutions directly.
result: The paper presents representative methods MSDPII, PSDWII, and PSDBP, claiming SDI complements and extends optimization-driven inversion and fills a gap in systematic presentation.
conclusion: Structure-driven inversion is proposed as a new paradigm for inverse problems, though the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Weighted Averages And Applications To Sets Of Multiple Recurrence
authors: Michael Reilly Vitaly Bergelson
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce new techniques for determining combinatorial properties of sets of multiple recurrence by considering weighted averages with quickly growing weights. Our main result is a far-reaching generalization of Szemer\'edi's Theorem which additionally confirms a conjecture of Bergelson-Moreira-Richter and contains as special cases both the Polynomial Szemer\'edi Theorem due to Bergelson-Leibman-Lesigne and the fact that if [MATH] belongs to a broad class of smooth functions and satisfies [MATH] for some [MATH] then for any [MATH], any invertible measure preserving system [MATH], and any [MATH] with [MATH], the set [MATH] is thick, meaning that it contains arbitrarily long intervals of natural numbers. Additionally, we formulate and prove a generalization to weighted averages of Boshernitzan's criterion for uniform distribution which we use in the proof of our main result.
tldr: This pure mathematics paper develops weighted averaging techniques to generalize Szemerédi's theorem and characterize sets of multiple recurrence, with no connection to quantum information science.
motivation: The work aims to determine combinatorial properties of sets of multiple recurrence and confirm a conjecture of Bergelson-Moreira-Richter, extending classical results in ergodic theory and combinatorics.
method: The authors introduce weighted averages with quickly growing weights and prove a generalization of Boshernitzan's criterion for uniform distribution to use in the main proof.
result: The main theorem is a far-reaching generalization of Szemerédi's theorem that includes the Polynomial Szemerédi Theorem and a thickness result for certain smooth functions as special cases.
conclusion: The paper advances pure ergodic theory and combinatorics but lies entirely outside the researcher's interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Resolution Of Friedgut's Conjecture On Influential Coalitions
authors: Mohit Gurumukhani Eshan Chattopadhyay
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for every constant [MATH] and every function [MATH], there is a coalition of [MATH] coordinates and a target output [MATH] such that, after the remaining coordinates are sampled uniformly and independently, the coalition can choose its values to make the output equal to [MATH] with probability at least [MATH]. The bound is independent of the alphabet size and also holds for monotone Boolean functions on [MATH], resolving a conjecture of Friedgut (Combinatorics, Probability and Computing, 2004). Unlike the Boolean cube setting, where Kahn, Kalai, and Linial (FOCS, 1988) give a coalition bound of [MATH], no sublinear bound independent of the alphabet size was previously known. In collective coin flipping, our result gives the first sublinear bound on the number of bad players needed to force a fixed output with probability at least [MATH] in any one-round protocol with independent uniform messages, regardless of the message length. A key ingredient in our proof is an encoding that lets us relate the influence of a function on a product space to the [MATH]-biased influence of the encoded function. We then rely on a structure theorem of Hatami (Annals of Mathematics, 2012) for functions with small [MATH]-biased influence to bias the encoded function.
tldr: The paper resolves Friedgut's conjecture by proving sublinear coalition bounds for Boolean functions on product spaces, independent of alphabet size.
motivation: Friedgut conjectured that influential coalitions of sublinear size can force a fixed output with constant probability, but prior bounds depended on alphabet size; this remained open for non-Boolean product spaces.
method: The proof introduces an encoding that relates influence on product spaces to the q-biased influence of an encoded function, then applies Hatami's structure theorem for functions with small q-biased influence.
result: For every constant q and function, there exists a coalition of o(n) coordinates that can force the output to a target value with probability at least a constant, independent of alphabet size; this also yields the first sublinear bound on bad players in one-round collective coin flipping.
conclusion: The work resolves a 2004 conjecture of Friedgut and establishes new sublinear bounds in collective coin flipping, advancing classical Boolean function analysis and influence theory.

title: Anchored Sequential Deliberation
authors: Ashish Goel Sijing Tu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequential deliberation is a mechanism for collective decision making: at each round, a uniformly randomly selected pair is asked to revise a collective outcome, which then becomes the reference point for the next round. Existing theory by Fain et al.~ treats the current outcome solely as the disagreement alternative in bargaining. Yet an existing draft, policy, or proposal might carry social influence and anchor participants' expressed positions toward the status quo. We introduce anchored sequential deliberation on a one-dimensional decision space. In each round, two participants with bliss points [MATH] and [MATH] shift their positions toward the previous outcome [MATH] with anchoring strength [MATH], then Nash-bargain using [MATH] as the disagreement alternative. The update simplifies to [MATH]. We establish a convergence--stability trade-off. For every population distribution and [MATH], the process has a unique stationary distribution. A monotone coupling yields a [MATH]-Wasserstein contraction factor of at most [MATH] and at least [MATH]; thus, stronger anchoring slows mixing. On the other hand, stationary social cost weakly decreases with [MATH], although the worst-case distortion remains [MATH]. We also identify a unique , where the expected unanchored movement is zero, and prove that the stationary distribution concentrates around it as [MATH]. For the uniform population, stationary distortion lies between [MATH] and [MATH], with both bounds approaching [MATH] as [MATH]. Simulations for uniform and Beta populations show that stronger anchoring slows mixing, concentrates the stationary distribution, and lowers stationary distortion in these instances.
tldr: The paper introduces 'anchored sequential deliberation', a model of collective decision making on a one-dimensional space where randomly selected pairs of participants anchor toward the previous outcome before Nash bargaining, and analyzes the resulting convergence–stability trade-off.
motivation: Existing theory of sequential deliberation treats the current outcome only as a disagreement alternative in bargaining, ignoring the possibility that an established draft, policy, or proposal exerts social influence that pulls participants' expressed positions toward the status quo.
method: The authors formalize a stochastic process in which each round a randomly chosen pair with bliss points shifts positions toward the previous outcome with anchoring strength, then Nash-bargains; they derive a simplified update rule and analyze it using monotone coupling and Wasserstein contraction techniques.
result: They prove a unique stationary distribution exists for every population distribution and anchoring strength, establish a Wasserstein contraction factor bounded above and below that increases with anchoring strength, show stationary social cost weakly decreases with anchoring while worst-case distortion remains constant, and identify a unique point of zero expected unanchored movement around which the stationary distribution concentrates.
conclusion: Stronger anchoring slows mixing but concentrates the stationary distribution and lowers stationary distortion, revealing a fundamental trade-off between convergence speed and stability; simulations for uniform and Beta populations confirm these findings.

title: Constant Swap Regret In General-Sum Games Via Optimistic Transition Matrices
authors: Tung Mai
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give deterministic and uncoupled learning dynamics for finite multiplayer general-sum games under full-information feedback that achieve constant individual swap regret, independent of the horizon [MATH]. With [MATH] players and at most [MATH] actions each, the individual swap regret of every player is [MATH] at every finite horizon. Each player predicts the deviation gains, then uses these predictions to update a row-stochastic transition matrix, and plays its stationary distribution. The proof combines a potential argument exploiting stationarity with a two-scale higher-order prediction analysis, using rooted-tree representations to handle the nonlinear dependence of deviation gains on the stationary distributions. An adversarially robust variant, obtained through a generic common-prefix switching wrapper, preserves the self-play bound up to a universal constant and guarantees individual swap regret at most [MATH] in the adversarial setting.
tldr: The paper presents deterministic uncoupled learning dynamics for finite multiplayer general-sum games that achieve constant individual swap regret independent of the time horizon.
motivation: The work addresses the challenge of obtaining horizon-independent regret guarantees in general-sum games, where standard no-regret dynamics often have regret growing with time.
method: Each player predicts deviation gains and uses them to update a row-stochastic transition matrix, playing its stationary distribution; the analysis combines a potential argument with two-scale higher-order prediction and rooted-tree representations.
result: With N players and at most m actions each, every player's individual swap regret is O(1) at every finite horizon, and an adversarially robust variant achieves regret at most O(√T) in the adversarial setting.
conclusion: The proposed optimistic transition matrix approach yields constant swap regret in self-play and provides a generic wrapper for adversarial robustness, advancing learning dynamics in general-sum games.

title: Gauged Aksz Sigma Models
authors: Noriaki Ikeda
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new class of sigma models that extend AKSZ sigma models, which we refer to as gauged AKSZ sigma models. These models are constructed using QP-manifolds. The compatibility between the AKSZ structure and gauging is characterized by geometric conditions on the target graded manifold. As an example, we explicitly analyze the gauging of higher Courant sigma models in higher dimensions. When fluxes and boundaries are introduced into gauged higher Courant sigma models, generalizations of momentum maps and Hamiltonian [MATH]-spaces arise as consistency conditions for the models.
tldr: The paper introduces gauged AKSZ sigma models using QP-manifolds and analyzes gauging of higher Courant sigma models with fluxes and boundaries.
motivation: The work aims to extend the AKSZ construction to gauged sigma models, providing a geometric framework for consistent gauging in higher-dimensional field theories.
method: It uses QP-manifolds and geometric conditions on the target graded manifold to characterize compatibility between AKSZ structure and gauging, exemplified by higher Courant sigma models.
result: The gauging procedure yields generalizations of momentum maps and Hamiltonian spaces as consistency conditions when fluxes and boundaries are included.
conclusion: Gauged AKSZ sigma models offer a broader mathematical framework for gauge theories, with higher Courant sigma models as a concrete application.

title: Two Preregistered Datasets On Production-type Labelling In The Entso-e Transparency Platform: Multi-fuel Reporting, Register Vintages, Persistent Misclassification, And Cross-product Consistency
authors: Eirik Botten Nicolaysen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ENTSO-E Transparency Platform is the single mandated publication point for European electricity market data, and three of its data items carry a production-type label. Commission Regulation (EU) No 543/2013 Article 16(1)(a) requires actual generation output per generation unit but does not mention production type; the label on that item is ENTSO-E's own addition through the schema, and Article 5(d) delegates the classification of production types to a Manual of Procedures. This data descriptor documents two preregistered datasets that measure what that classification does in practice, along four axes: simultaneous multi-fuel reporting, type change between capacity-register vintages, persistent misclassification without type change, and cross-product consistency between the per-unit and the aggregated series. Criteria were locked and checksummed before measurement, thresholds are derived from measured noise rather than chosen, and what did not survive is recorded: six claims are withdrawn, three of them from published versions of the datasets themselves. Across 2191 documents covering 199 generation units in three bidding zones where biomass co-firing is documented in a dated primary source, no unit carries two production types in the same document. One practical warning applies to every user of the hourly series: all of it carries curveType A03, a step curve in which a missing position means the previous value holds rather than that data are absent. A parser that sums only the points listed under-reports energy unevenly, by 22.6 percent for one Finnish unit in 2021.
tldr: This data descriptor documents two preregistered datasets auditing the consistency and correctness of production-type labels in the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform's European electricity market data.
motivation: Commission Regulation (EU) No 543/2013 delegates production-type classification to ENTSO-E's own schema and Manual of Procedures, leaving the practical behavior of that labelling unmeasured and potentially misleading for data users.
method: Criteria were locked and checksummed before measurement, with thresholds derived from measured noise; four axes were probed — simultaneous multi-fuel reporting, type change across capacity-register vintages, persistent misclassification, and cross-product consistency — across 2191 documents covering 199 generation units in three bidding zones.
result: No unit carries two production types in the same document; six claims were withdrawn (three from previously published dataset versions); and curveType A03 (step curve) causes naive parsers to under-report energy unevenly, by 22.6 percent for one Finnish unit in 2021.
conclusion: The work provides a preregistered, reproducibility-focused audit of energy-market metadata quality and warns all users of the hourly series that step-curve semantics must be handled correctly.

title: Ultimate Performance Of Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Mach-Zehnder Modulators
authors: Shiva Behzadfar, Fatemeh Karami, Pooja Kulkarni, Sasan Fathpour
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In thin-film lithium niobate Mach-Zehnder modulators, half-wave voltage and bandwidth are tied to the same design parameters; hence, improving one usually costs the other. Several methods have been pursued in the past to alleviate this tradeoff. Specifically, the bias voltage can be reduced through non-centered placement of optical waveguides with respect to electrodes, slow-wave optical gratings, and high-permittivity cladding layers. Bandwidth can be enhanced through implementing periodic segmented electrodes and exploiting low-permittivity bottom cladding and substrate materials. The objective of this work is to study the augmentative impact of these methods. We pursue a rigorous modeling and optimization approach to achieve this objective, estimate the impact of each augmentation, and evaluate the ultimate performance of TFLN MZMs based on these methods. It is shown that a co-designed structure that incorporates all these enhancing methods can attain a drive voltage of 0.84 V and a modulation bandwidth of almost 220 GHz.
tldr: A modeling and optimization study of thin-film lithium niobate Mach-Zehnder modulators that co-designs several voltage- and bandwidth-enhancing techniques to project ultimate device performance.
motivation: Half-wave voltage and bandwidth in TFLN Mach-Zehnder modulators are coupled through shared design parameters, so improving one typically degrades the other; prior work has proposed various mitigation methods whose combined impact had not been systematically quantified.
method: The authors build a rigorous electro-optic modeling and optimization framework for TFLN MZM structures, individually quantifying the effect of non-centered waveguide placement, slow-wave optical gratings, high-permittivity claddings, segmented electrodes, and low-permittivity bottom cladding/substrate.
result: A co-designed structure incorporating all enhancing methods is predicted to achieve a drive voltage of 0.84 V together with a modulation bandwidth of nearly 220 GHz.
conclusion: The paper shows that combining multiple design augmentations can substantially relax the voltage–bandwidth tradeoff in TFLN modulators, providing performance targets for future high-speed electro-optic devices.

title: Unsupervised Machine Learning Of The Contact Process
authors: L. T. Brito, G. A. Alves, F. W. S. Lima, A. Macedo-Filho, R. S. Ferreira, T. F. A. Alves
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how unsupervised machine-learning methods can characterize the active-absorbing phase transition in the contact process in one and two spatial dimensions. Our analysis focuses on principal component analysis (PCA) and variational autoencoders (VAEs), and we show that direct applications of these methods encounter a central difficulty: contact process configurations are intrinsically positive-definite. In the PCA case, standard centering procedures fail to isolate the order parameter in the leading component. To address this, we augment the data with sign-reversed configurations, creating a balanced dataset with zero mean while preserving the density information required to describe the transition. This preprocessing allows the dominant principal component to recover the order parameter and reproduce the expected finite-size scaling near criticality. For VAEs, we find a related limitation: a fixed Gaussian prior does not provide sufficient latent regularization across the full range of control parameters and system sizes for positive-definite data. We overcome this by adopting a heteroscedastic Gaussian prior that adapts to the control parameter, leading to a substantial improvement in the finite-size scaling of reconstruction-based observables near the critical threshold. Taken together, these results highlight a key lesson: the success of machine learning in phase-transition problems does not rely on algorithmic complexity alone, but on tailoring the representation to respect the physical structure of the system, including its intrinsic constraints and symmetries.
tldr: Unsupervised machine learning (PCA and VAEs) is used to characterize the active-absorbing phase transition in the classical contact process, with preprocessing tailored to positive-definite configurations.
motivation: The authors investigate whether unsupervised methods can detect the contact process phase transition and address the difficulty that its configurations are intrinsically positive-definite.
method: They apply PCA with sign-reversed data augmentation to create a zero-mean balanced dataset, and VAEs with a heteroscedastic Gaussian prior that adapts to the control parameter, in one and two spatial dimensions.
result: Sign-reversal preprocessing lets the leading principal component recover the order parameter and finite-size scaling, while the adaptive prior substantially improves reconstruction-based observables near criticality.
conclusion: The success of machine learning in phase-transition problems depends on tailoring the representation to respect the physical structure, constraints, and symmetries of the system.

title: On The Reconstruction Of Sas From Other Triangle Congruence Criteria
authors: Roberto Volpe
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Starting from a Hilbert plane and removing the Side-Angle-Side (SAS) congruence axiom, we investigate to what extent SAS can be recovered synthetically from the remaining classical triangle congruence criteria. We show that the Angle-Side-Angle criterion, together with a ray correspondence principle corresponding to Theorem 13 of Hilbert's , suffices to reconstruct SAS. We further show that both the Side-Side-Side and the Side-Angle-Angle criteria also suffice, once combined with the ray correspondence principle and suitable auxiliary principles -- the existence of midpoints and a hypotenuse-angle criterion for right triangles in the first case, and the existence of angle bisectors, the congruence of supplements of congruent angles, and the Pons Asinorum in the second. Although the two routes rely on auxiliary principles of different character, we show that they converge on a single final argument once a common hypotenuse-angle criterion is established. A metamathematical analysis, based on an explicit model adapted from Hilbert's own independence construction, complements these reconstructions: it shows that the ray correspondence principle alone cannot reconstruct any of the classical criteria, and that the Pons Asinorum and the hypotenuse-angle criterion are each independent of the remaining auxiliary principles used in their respective reconstructions. The resulting picture is not a formal hierarchy of the congruence criteria, but it does show that the Angle-Side-Angle reconstruction rests on a provably more economical basis than those obtained from Side-Side-Side or Side-Angle-Angle.
tldr: The paper investigates whether the Side-Angle-Side (SAS) congruence axiom of Hilbert plane geometry can be synthetically reconstructed from the remaining classical triangle congruence criteria, showing that Angle-Side-Angle plus a ray correspondence principle suffices and forms a provably more economical basis.
motivation: Hilbert's axiomatization of Euclidean geometry takes SAS as a foundational congruence axiom, and the author asks how essential this axiom is relative to the other classical triangle congruence criteria.
method: The author performs synthetic geometric derivations within a Hilbert plane lacking SAS, combining ASA, SSS, and SAA criteria with auxiliary principles (midpoints, angle bisectors, hypotenuse-angle criterion, Pons Asinorum, supplement congruence), and complements these with a metamathematical independence analysis using an explicit model adapted from Hilbert's independence construction.
result: ASA together with a ray correspondence principle reconstructs SAS; SSS and SAA also suffice when combined with the ray correspondence principle and suitable auxiliary principles, with all routes converging on a common hypotenuse-angle argument, while the metamathematical model shows the ray correspondence principle alone cannot reconstruct any classical criterion and that Pons Asinorum and the hypotenuse-angle criterion are mutually independent of the other auxiliary principles.
conclusion: The reconstructions do not yield a formal hierarchy of the congruence criteria, but they demonstrate that the Angle-Side-Angle route to SAS rests on a provably more economical axiomatic basis than the Side-Side-Side or Side-Angle-Angle routes.

title: The Fixed-point Bundle Method Over Product-of-simplex Domains Arising From Game Equilibria
authors: Hongbo Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper extends the fixed-point bundle framework for finite-dimensional variational inequalities (VIs) from the simplex domain to the product-of-simplex domain, which is directly applicable to solving Nash equilibria. The fixed-point bundle for VIs on the product-of-simplex domain reveals a composite fiber bundle structure. The key innovation is to construct an equivalent VI on the simplex domain and establish the equivalence between the two fixed-point bundle frameworks via a fiber bundle isomorphism. Exploiting this geometric equivalence, the predictor-corrector path-following algorithm for the VI on the product-of-simplex domain is shown to inherit the convergence guarantee of the simplex-domain framework, namely, global convergence with linear gap reduction near solutions. Numerical experiments on 5600 randomly generated instances with dimensions ranging from 2-player 128-action to 128-player 2-action demonstrate robust performance. The algorithm converges in every tested instance.
tldr: This paper develops a fixed-point bundle method for variational inequalities over product-of-simplex domains, with application to Nash equilibria.
motivation: The work aims to extend fixed-point bundle algorithms from simplex domains to product-of-simplex domains, enabling efficient computation of Nash equilibria in games.
method: It constructs an equivalent variational inequality on the simplex domain and uses a fiber bundle isomorphism to transfer convergence guarantees to the product-of-simplex setting.
result: The predictor-corrector path-following algorithm achieves global convergence with linear gap reduction, as demonstrated on 5600 randomly generated instances up to 128 players or actions.
conclusion: The proposed geometric equivalence provides a principled algorithmic framework for solving Nash equilibria via fixed-point bundles on product-of-simplex domains.

title: Asymptotic Separation Of Periodic Orbits And Fractal Dimension
authors: Derong Kong, Zhiqiang Wang, Daohua Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a totally bounded metric dynamical system [MATH] we introduce a new critical value [MATH] which quantifies the asymptotic separation of periodic orbits. More precisely, [MATH] is defined to be the supremum of all [MATH] for which there exists a sequence of periodic orbits [MATH] in [MATH] such that \[ \lim_{k\to \infty} \#\mathcal O_k = +\infty \quad \quad \liminf_{k\to\infty}\#\mathcal O_k\cdot\eta(\mathcal O_k)^s >0, \] where [MATH] denotes the smallest distance between distinct points in [MATH]. When the dynamical system is induced by a self-similar iterated function system [MATH] satisfying the strong separation condition, we prove that this critical value is equal to the Hausdorff dimension [MATH] of its self-similar attractor. Furthermore, under a quantitative separation condition on periodic orbits we show that the associated empirical periodic measures converge weakly to the normalized [MATH]-dimensional Hausdorff measure on the self-similar attractor.
tldr: The paper introduces a critical value quantifying asymptotic separation of periodic orbits and relates it to the Hausdorff dimension of self-similar attractors.
motivation: Periodic orbits and their separation properties are central to understanding the geometry and dynamics of fractal sets, but a quantitative link to fractal dimension was lacking.
method: The authors define a critical exponent based on the growth and minimal separation of periodic orbits, and analyze self-similar iterated function systems satisfying the strong separation condition.
result: They prove the critical value equals the Hausdorff dimension of the self-similar attractor, and under a quantitative separation condition, empirical periodic measures converge weakly to the normalized Hausdorff measure.
conclusion: This establishes a new asymptotic characterization of fractal dimension via periodic orbit statistics, with implications for the ergodic theory of self-similar sets.

title: Non-uniqueness Of Characteristic Curves Of Folding Rational Maps
authors: Jinsong Zeng Luxian Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A folding rational map is a postcritically finite rational map [MATH] admitting an essential Jordan curve [MATH], disjoint from the postcritical set [MATH], whose preimage is disconnected and consists of Jordan curves homotopic to [MATH] relative to [MATH]. Such [MATH] is called a characteristic curve of [MATH]. We construct a real postcritically finite rational map [MATH] of degree [MATH] with [MATH], which admits two non-homotopic characteristic curves [MATH] and [MATH]. It is hyperbolic with orbifold signature [MATH]. This non-uniqueness is not a Latt\`es phenomenon, nor does it arise from a mating decomposition. The map is constructed piecewise, and a numerical model is provided to illustrate its dynamics. Thurston obstructions are excluded by arc-lifting and intersection-number arguments.
tldr: The paper constructs a real postcritically finite rational map of degree 4 admitting two non-homotopic characteristic curves, showing non-uniqueness of characteristic curves for folding rational maps.
motivation: Characteristic curves of folding rational maps had been implicitly assumed unique; the authors aim to test whether this uniqueness fails in the postcritically finite setting.
method: A piecewise construction of a hyperbolic degree-4 rational map with orbifold signature (0;2,2,2,4) is given, with Thurston obstructions excluded via arc-lifting and intersection-number arguments, plus a numerical model.
result: The constructed map admits two non-homotopic characteristic curves, and this non-uniqueness is shown not to stem from a Lattès phenomenon or a mating decomposition.
conclusion: Uniqueness of characteristic curves does not hold in general for folding rational maps, and the paper's techniques may be useful for classifying such maps and their associated obstructions.

title: Permutation-Based Stegomalware In Large Language Models: Threats And Countermeasures
authors: James Stringer Danny Wood
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The difficulty of training large language models (LLMs), together with their ubiquity, raises the threat of stegomalware, where malicious payloads are embedded into model weights. Recent work has demonstrated the use of permutation symmetry in model weights to mitigate these threats, but failed to show neutralization of stegomalware across all weights for LLMs. In this paper, we demonstrate the full potential of behavior-preserving symmetries as a defense against stegomalware, as well as the risks these symmetries pose when exploited by attackers. For stegomalware neutralization, we improve upon previous work, demonstrating that it is possible to select permutations which displace all model parameters. This contrasts with previous methods which left a significant percentage of weights unaltered in LLMs. When used in an attack, we show that permutation symmetries can encode malware into the weights of a model in a way that is theoretically lossless, requires no retraining after encoding, and needs no payload-specific information in the extraction script---a combination of characteristics not previously seen in any single method. While theoretically lossless, permutation can in practice alter model behavior due to the accumulation of numerical error. We therefore quantify the loss in model performance associated with applying these methods, for both attack and defense, showing it to be minimal.
tldr: This paper studies permutation-based stegomalware in large language models, showing how weight permutations can both neutralize and embed malicious payloads with minimal performance loss.
motivation: The ubiquity and training difficulty of LLMs create a threat surface for stegomalware embedded in model weights, and prior permutation defenses did not fully neutralize all parameters.
method: The authors use behavior-preserving permutation symmetries in LLM weights, selecting permutations that displace all model parameters, and quantify numerical error and performance loss for attack and defense.
result: They demonstrate full parameter displacement for stegomalware neutralization and show that permutation can encode theoretically lossless malware without retraining or payload-specific extraction information, with only minimal practical performance degradation.
conclusion: Permutation symmetries offer a powerful dual-use tool for LLM stegomalware, improving defenses while also enabling new attack vectors, with numerical error being the main practical limitation.

title: Understanding The Usability Of Cryptographic Verification Tools
authors: Tarikul Islam, Yasin Islam, Khandakar Ashrafi Akbar, Imtiaz Karim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cryptographic protocol verification tools are widely used to analyze the security of complex protocols, yet how users interact with these tools remains comparatively understudied. We present an exploratory human-centered study of experienced users of Tamarin, ProVerif, and related protocol verifiers. Our survey included researchers, graduate students, and practitioners with hands-on experience using Tamarin, ProVerif, or related tools. The findings reveal usability barriers across the verification workflow, including difficulties debugging non-termination and performance issues, and the lack of systematic methods for validating formal models against real protocols. When proofs fail without concrete attacks, users commonly simplify models, add helper lemmas, and revisit modeling abstractions. Participants also called for actionable diagnostics, clearer explanations of results, visualization, and automation for recurring proof tasks. Our findings suggest that persistent usability challenges arise from the gap between protocol-level reasoning and the verifier's formal model, proof procedures, and diagnostic output. We derive concrete design priorities for improving the accessibility, interpretability, and usability of cryptographic protocol verification tools.
tldr: An exploratory human-centered study of experienced users of cryptographic protocol verification tools such as Tamarin and ProVerif, identifying usability barriers and design priorities.
motivation: Cryptographic protocol verification tools are widely used but how users interact with them is understudied, motivating investigation into practical usability issues.
method: The authors conducted a survey of researchers, graduate students, and practitioners with hands-on experience using Tamarin, ProVerif, or related protocol verifiers.
result: Users face barriers debugging non-termination and performance issues, lack systematic methods to validate formal models against real protocols, and often simplify models or add helper lemmas when proofs fail without concrete attacks.
conclusion: The study derives concrete design priorities to improve accessibility, interpretability, and usability of cryptographic protocol verification tools.

title: gr-PHYSEC: Real-time Channel-based Key Generation For Physical Layer Secure Wireless Communications
authors: Jose Angel Sanchez Viloria, George Sklivanitis, Dimitris Pados
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Securing wireless communication against eavesdropping is critical, particularly in dynamic and decentralized environments. We present gr-PHYSEC, a new GNU Radio out-of-tree (OOT) module for real-time physical-layer key generation. Unlike traditional key generation that relies on pre-shared secrets or computational complexity, our approach derives symmetric keys from the wireless channel's inherent randomness. We embed a trained neural network within GNU Radio to extract channel features between trusted parties (Alice and Bob) during probe exchanges. These features are quantized into binary keys, reconciled via Reed-Solomon encoding, and further secured with SHA-512 hashing. The generated keys are then directly used to encrypt data. Real-world experiments at the FAU CAAI connected robotics testbed using ADALM Pluto software-defined radios and NVIDIA Jetson Orin validate the approach with ground robotic platforms. Results demonstrate low key disagreement rates and strong randomness, as verified by the NIST test suite for random and pseudorandom number generators for cryptographic applications. This integration showcases how GNU Radio can support real-time AI-driven security solutions, pushing the boundaries of software-defined secure communication. The source code for this project is available at: [URL].
tldr: gr-PHYSEC is a GNU Radio out-of-tree module that generates symmetric encryption keys in real time from the inherent randomness of wireless channels using neural network feature extraction and cryptographic reconciliation.
motivation: Securing wireless communication against eavesdropping in dynamic and decentralized environments is critical, and traditional key generation relying on pre-shared secrets or computational complexity is insufficient.
method: The system embeds a trained neural network within GNU Radio to extract channel features between trusted parties during probe exchanges, quantizes these features into binary keys, reconciles them via Reed-Solomon encoding, and secures them with SHA-512 hashing before direct use for encryption.
result: Real-world experiments at the FAU CAAI testbed using ADALM Pluto software-defined radios and NVIDIA Jetson Orin with ground robotic platforms demonstrate low key disagreement rates and strong randomness, as verified by the NIST test suite.
conclusion: The work showcases how GNU Radio can support real-time AI-driven physical-layer security for wireless communications, but it is a classical wireless security contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cross-Domain Inference For Human Localization: Applying Wi-Fi Rssi Data To CSI-Trained Models
authors: Ariel Duschanek-Myers, Thomas Welsh, Helmut Neukirchen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wi-Fi signal data can be used to compromise the privacy of individuals. While many existing approaches rely on Channel State Information (CSI), collecting this data on typical IoT devices often requires elevated operating system permissions and specialized drivers. Consequently, this paper investigates the feasibility of utilizing Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) data to predict human locations. RSSI was selected because it is accessible even on devices with limited user permissions, and therefore is more applicable to a wider array of IoT devices. To bypass the tedious process of obtaining training data needed to train an RSSI-based model, an existing Wi-Fi pose prediction project was used in this research. However, that project assumed CSI data as input. Therefore, we investigate the feasibility of cross-domain inference, i.e., feeding RSSI data into that existing CSI-based model. We collected an RSSI dataset, synchronized with video ground-truth of a person moving within a room, to evaluate the model's performance. This evaluation confirmed that RSSI data can predict locations with approximately 80% confidence when human movement is present. This demonstrates that a model trained on CSI data can be used to evaluate low-granularity RSSI data consisting of decibel-milliwatt (dBm) values to roughly locate people in the collection space. These results imply that a wide range of IoT devices can be used for privacy invasion in Wi-Fi-dense environments.
tldr: The paper shows that a model trained on Wi-Fi CSI data can be repurposed to infer human locations from low-granularity RSSI measurements, achieving roughly 80% accuracy.
motivation: Wi-Fi-based human localization typically relies on CSI, which requires elevated permissions and specialized drivers on IoT devices, limiting applicability. RSSI is broadly accessible and could enable wider deployment for privacy-invasive localization.
method: The authors collected an RSSI dataset synchronized with video ground truth of a person moving in a room and performed cross-domain inference by feeding RSSI data into an existing CSI-trained Wi-Fi pose prediction model.
result: Cross-domain inference succeeded: RSSI data predicted human locations with approximately 80% confidence when human movement was present, despite the model being trained only on CSI.
conclusion: The findings suggest that a wide range of permission-limited IoT devices can leverage RSSI with CSI-trained models for privacy invasion in Wi-Fi-dense environments, raising notable privacy concerns.

title: Towards Digital Halftoning On Closed Manifolds--An Error Diffusion Scheme For The $2d$ Torus Based On Sigma-Delta Quantization Along The Rank-one Lattice
authors: Alessandro Lupoli Felix Krahmer
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital halftoning aims to represent continuous-tone images by binary patterns while preserving their visually relevant low-frequency content. Among the many available approaches, error-diffusion methods implement noise shaping through causal feedback filters and can be interpreted as two-dimensional versions of the signal quantization paradigm Sigma--Delta modulation. On closed domains, however, the terminal state of the underlying recurrence relation need not match the initial one, producing boundary artifacts. We study this problem for bandlimited functions on the two-dimensional torus. By arranging all pixels along a single closed rank-one lattice, we replace the multiple mismatches associated with separately processed rows and columns with a single terminal contribution, while retaining exact reconstruction. For a uniform lattice with \(N=M^2+1\) points, we obtain first- and second-order error bounds of order \(N^{-1/2}\) and \(N^{-1}\). A suitable constant update eliminates the terminal mismatch and reduces the spatial localization of the error without changing these asymptotic orders. For fixed-direction rank-one lattices, the corrected first- and second-order reconstructions instead achieve rates \(N^{-1}\) and \(N^{-2}\). Numerical experiments illustrate a reduction in boundary artifacts compared with classical schemes applied on the Cartesian grid.
tldr: The paper develops an error-diffusion halftoning scheme for bandlimited functions on the 2D torus using sigma-delta quantization along a rank-one lattice to reduce boundary artifacts.
motivation: On closed domains, standard error diffusion suffers terminal mismatch causing boundary artifacts; there is a need for a scheme that preserves exact reconstruction while reducing such artifacts.
method: All pixels are arranged along a single closed rank-one lattice, replacing multiple row/column mismatches with one terminal contribution; first- and second-order error bounds are derived, and a constant update eliminates the terminal mismatch.
result: For a uniform lattice with N=M^2+1 points, error bounds of order N^{-1/2} and N^{-1} are obtained; for fixed-direction rank-one lattices, corrected first- and second-order reconstructions achieve rates N^{-1} and N^{-2}, with numerical experiments showing reduced boundary artifacts.
conclusion: The rank-one lattice approach provides a principled way to mitigate boundary artifacts in halftoning on closed manifolds, with improved asymptotic rates for fixed directions, though the work is classical signal processing and outside quantum information interests.

title: Simulating Multimode Nonlinearities At Very High Mode Count Via Parallel Factor Decomposition
authors: Nicholas Rivera
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A variety of problems at the frontier of nonlinear optics involve strongly multimode interactions. Simulating these dynamics is often computationally challenging due to the complexity of evaluating a large number of nonlinear overlaps. This is especially acute in ultrafast Kerr effect physics, where simulations in a modal representation have a generic complexity scaling quartically with the number of modes. This has limited the largest number of modes retainable in simulations in practice to a few tens of modes (often fewer), even when run on modern GPUs. Here, I show how by taking advantage of parallel factor decompositions of the nonlinear overlap tensor, a far larger number of modes can be accommodated. Realistic values for generic index profiles without special symmetries or separability can be in the thousands, and with special symmetries, far larger. I show that simulations with [MATH]1,000 modes can be done on modern hardware, illustrating this with the example of a multimode soliton propagating over a meter of GRIN fiber. I further show that the improved scaling immediately makes it practical to consider statistical effects, illustrating with the example of noise amplification in soliton fission. These results, implemented in public code with examples, should enable access to simulating the most demanding regimes of multimode nonlinear optics. Compression of the nonlinear interaction tensor may provide a route for more efficient simulation of nonlinear wave dynamics across a variety of other systems including acoustics, water waves, phononics, magnonics, and Bose condensates.
tldr: A computational method based on parallel factor decomposition is introduced to efficiently simulate multimode nonlinear optical interactions with thousands of modes.
motivation: Simulating strongly multimode nonlinear optics, especially ultrafast Kerr effects, is computationally prohibitive due to quartic scaling of nonlinear overlap evaluations, limiting practical simulations to a few tens of modes.
method: The nonlinear overlap tensor is decomposed using parallel factor decomposition, dramatically reducing the complexity of evaluating multimode nonlinear interactions without requiring special symmetries.
result: Simulations with over 1,000 modes are demonstrated on modern hardware, including a multimode soliton propagating over a meter of GRIN fiber and statistical noise amplification in soliton fission.
conclusion: Tensor compression enables access to previously intractable regimes of multimode nonlinear optics and may generalize to other nonlinear wave systems such as acoustics, water waves, phononics, magnonics, and Bose condensates.

title: Learning Transferable Self-Supervised Priors For Super-Resolution Reconstruction In Structured Illumination Microscopy
authors: Tong-Tian Weng, Ze-Hao Wang, Qi Wang, Xi-Hua Wang, Xiang-Dong Chen, Fang-Wen Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structured illumination microscopy (SIM) extends the optical passband, and reconstruction of detail beyond it depends on prior knowledge. Hand-designed regularizers depend on how well their structural assumptions match the specimen; learned priors can be sensitive to changes in imaging conditions and specimen structure. We introduce SIMAdapter, which pretrains a network that predicts the emitter and the point-spread function (PSF) by self-supervision on 23,237 raw SIM stacks from BioSR, BioTISR, and simulations spanning different PSFs and specimen structures, then adapts it to a single unlabeled target stack. Adaptation refines the network against a differentiable image-formation model, with the light pattern calibrated from that stack. Both stages take their supervision from the raw measurements and need no paired high-resolution reference. On two held-out synthetic domains, SIMAdapter reaches a mean emitter normalized root-mean-square error of 0.156, compared with 0.403 for Sparse-SIM. The same adaptation started from a network pretrained on BioSR alone is less accurate in both domains. In three experimental case studies, adaptation reduces flanking artifacts and yields more distinct profiles across filament pairs, mitochondrial boundaries, and calibration lines. A single pretrained network can thus be reused across SIM measurements, with each reconstruction refined against its own raw data.
tldr: SIMAdapter is a self-supervised transfer learning method for structured illumination microscopy super-resolution reconstruction that pretrains on large raw SIM datasets and adapts to individual unlabeled stacks using a differentiable image-formation model.
motivation: Existing hand-designed regularizers for SIM reconstruction are sensitive to specimen structure, while learned priors often fail under changes in imaging conditions and specimen type.
method: The method pretrains a network to predict emitter and PSF from raw SIM stacks via self-supervision, then adapts it to a single unlabeled target stack by optimizing against a differentiable image-formation model with the illumination pattern calibrated from that stack.
result: On held-out synthetic domains, SIMAdapter achieves mean emitter NRMSE of 0.156 versus 0.403 for Sparse-SIM, and in experimental cases reduces flanking artifacts and improves profile distinction for filaments, mitochondrial boundaries, and calibration lines.
conclusion: A single pretrained network can be reused across SIM measurements, with each reconstruction refined against its own raw data, eliminating the need for paired high-resolution references.

title: Newton Geometry Of Bogdanov-Takens Degeneracies In Integrable Dilatonic Models: Invariant Divisors And Boundary Multiplicity
authors: E. Chan-L\'opez, A. Mart\'in-Ruiz, J. M. Paulin Fuentes

For [MATH] it has two distinct rank-one nilpotent equilibria with complementary Bogdanov--Takens (BT) degeneracies: [MATH] with multiplicity [MATH], and [MATH] with [MATH]. We show that this complementarity is forced by a single divisor-organized structure. The system is Darboux integrable, [MATH], where [MATH] is the mass function and [MATH] is an inverse integrating factor whose zero divisor is the invariant axis [MATH]. Off the divisor, every nilpotent equilibrium of [MATH] with [MATH] has [MATH], from [MATH]. On the divisor, invariance of the coordinate axis forces [MATH] because [MATH] and both factors vanish at the corner. tldr: The paper analyzes Bogdanov-Takens degeneracies in an integrable two-dimensional dilaton gravity model using Newton geometry and invariant divisors, showing that a versal two-parameter unfolding is impossible and computing local multiplicities.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structure of nilpotent equilibria and their multiplicities in a Kantowski-Sachs reduction of Grumiller's dilaton gravity model.
method: They use Darboux integrability, inverse integrating factors, invariant divisors, Bernstein-Kushnirenko bounds, and mixed-covolume interpretations to study the local geometry of the degeneracies.

conclusion: The findings establish constraints on BT unfoldings in this class and provide a detailed geometric classification, while leaving a general theorem for non-convenient diagrams open.

title: Reconstruction Through A Coisotropic Reduction: The Missing Momentum On A Poincar\'e Section As A Branched Covering
authors: E. Chan-L\'opez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining the momentum missing on a Poincar\'e section of a two-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian is usually posed as the root-finding problem [MATH], which degenerates at the boundary of the energetically allowed region. We argue that the degeneration is the visible symptom of a geometric object and reorganize the problem around it. The section is a coisotropic hypersurface, the missing momentum is its characteristic direction, and recovering it is a through the associated coisotropic reduction. Its carrier is not the fibrewise least-energy function, which we show is informationally incomplete, but the correspondence [MATH] together with the reducing projection [MATH], a branched reconstruction over the admissible region whose discriminant is identified with the Hill boundary under a base-side regularity condition. We prove, isolating for each conclusion its minimal hypothesis: that [MATH] is proper and a covering away from the discriminant (coercivity); that the fibres have exactly two points over the interior (unimodality); that along the discriminant [MATH] is a fold (fibrewise nondegeneracy and transversality); and that the discriminant coincides with the topological boundary of the admissible region precisely under a regularity of the least-energy function , which no fibrewise hypothesis supplies. Strict convexity of [MATH] in the momenta is shown to be a sufficient but non-fundamental bundle of these conditions. The boundary is a discriminant, not a Lagrangian caustic. Only afterwards does the squared fibrewise energy residual [MATH] appear, as the analytic resolution of the fold; inside the admissible region it is a double well with two global minimizers, so branch selection is a separate rule.
tldr: The paper recasts the problem of recovering the missing momentum on a Poincaré section as a coisotropic reduction whose reconstruction is a branched covering with discriminant at the Hill boundary.
motivation: Determining the missing momentum on a Poincaré section in two-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian systems is usually a root-finding problem that degenerates at the boundary of the energetically allowed region.
method: The authors identify the Poincaré section as a coisotropic hypersurface and the missing momentum as its characteristic direction, then use coisotropic reduction and branched covering theory under minimal hypotheses such as coercivity, unimodality, and fold conditions.
result: They prove that the correspondence and reducing projection form a branched reconstruction over the admissible region, with the discriminant coinciding with the Hill boundary under a base-side regularity condition, and show that strict convexity in momenta is sufficient but not fundamental.
conclusion: The boundary is a discriminant rather than a Lagrangian caustic, and the squared fibrewise energy residual emerges as the analytic resolution of the fold, with branch selection requiring a separate rule.

title: No Bit Left Behind: Using Brute-Force Lifting To Achieve Fully Static Binary Recompilation
authors: Tianjiao Huang, Po-An Chen, Nick Baron, Michael Franz
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binary recompilation is a technique for operating directly on executable code. It promises to automate two important tasks: retrofitting security mitigations onto legacy binaries, and migrating binaries across instruction set architectures (ISAs). Yet today, there is no fully automated system that can reliably lift arbitrary binary executables to a compiler intermediate representation (IR) such as LLVM IR, or that can fully statically and reliably translate non-trivial binary executables from one ISA to another. The main underlying problem is that recovering a program's control flow graph (CFG) statically is impossible in general: computed branches can jump to targets that cannot be determined without actually running the program. Existing systems resort to runtime fallback mechanisms, requiring a significant portion of the binary translation machinery to accompany the translated program on the target machine. This article presents a fully static, whole-program binary lifting system requiring no runtime translation support on the target. Rather than attempting to distinguish code from data, we treat every byte offset as a potential branch target and lift the entire binary in a brute-force manner, constructing a superset CFG that conservatively contains all feasible control flows. Statically unresolvable computed branches are thereby reduced to lookups in a dispatch table that points to the corresponding translated control flow path. We have implemented this approach as a prototype binary recompiler from x86-64 binaries to LLVM IR, requiring no code/data heuristics. We validate it with a fully static cross-compilation to AArch64, achieved by reusing existing LLVM backends with no modification.
tldr: The paper presents a fully static binary recompilation system that lifts entire x86-64 executables to LLVM IR by treating every byte offset as a potential branch target and building a conservative superset control-flow graph.
motivation: Existing binary lifting and ISA translation tools rely on runtime fallback because static recovery of a program's control flow graph is impossible in general due to computed branches, preventing fully automated and static recompilation.
method: The authors brute-force lift every byte offset of a binary, constructing a superset CFG that conservatively contains all feasible control flows and reduces unresolvable computed branches to dispatch-table lookups, implemented as an x86-64 to LLVM IR recompiler with no code/data heuristics.
result: The prototype achieves fully static whole-program lifting with no runtime translation support and is validated through cross-compilation from x86-64 to AArch64 by reusing unmodified existing LLVM backends.
conclusion: Brute-force lifting offers a practical route to fully static binary recompilation and ISA migration, eliminating the runtime overhead and target-side machinery required by prior dynamic approaches.

title: Rosetta: Efficient And Accurate Privacy-Preserving Llm Decoding Via Hybrid Ckks/tfhe Evaluation
authors: Jiangrui Yu, Baosheng Zhang, Liang Kong, Lin Ding, Yi Chen, Ye Yu, Mingzhe Zhang, Meng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative large language models (LLMs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance on many real-world tasks such as code generation and question answering. These models predominantly rely on an autoregressive decoding strategy that generates output tokens sequentially. However, their pervasive deployment raises serious privacy concerns, motivating private inference frameworks based on fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). A major limitation of existing FHE frameworks is their inefficiency in evaluating nonlinear operations, which incur substantial overhead and dominate the decode stage. In this paper, we propose ROSETTA, a hybrid CKKS/TFHE framework that overcomes this limitation. We first observe that nonlinear operations in the decode stage exhibit heterogeneous workload patterns, which can be handled effectively via a hybrid approach. We then realize this with two key contributions: 1) an adaptive segmented lookup-table protocol based on TFHE that enables efficient and accurate evaluation of nonlinear operations; and 2) a scheme-aware operator-selection framework that automatically assigns each nonlinear operator to CKKS or TFHE to minimize end-to-end decoding latency. We demonstrate that ROSETTA achieves up to [MATH] Softmax speedup and [MATH]--[MATH] end-to-end speedup over the SOTA framework CacheMir.
tldr: Rosetta presents a hybrid CKKS/TFHE framework for efficient and accurate privacy-preserving LLM decoding via fully homomorphic encryption.
motivation: Generative LLMs raise privacy concerns in deployment, and existing FHE-based private inference frameworks are inefficient in evaluating nonlinear operations during autoregressive decoding.
method: The authors exploit heterogeneous workload patterns in nonlinear operations and introduce an adaptive segmented lookup-table protocol based on TFHE along with a scheme-aware operator-selection framework that assigns operators to CKKS or TFHE.
result: Rosetta achieves up to significant Softmax speedup and 1-2 orders of magnitude end-to-end speedup over the state-of-the-art framework CacheMir.
conclusion: The hybrid approach demonstrates that combining CKKS and TFHE can substantially improve the practicality of privacy-preserving LLM inference.

title: N-tuple-periodic Solutions Of The Navier-Stokes Equations: Existence And Obstructions
authors: R. K. Michael Thambynayagam
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a phase-angle framework for constructing and classifying n-tuple-periodic solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, and use it to determine, dimension by dimension, when such solutions exist and why they fail. The velocity field is a difference of two n-fold cyclic trigonometric products, made divergence-free for every phase and every n >= 3 by a telescoping identity. The problem then reduces to two explicit conditions on the n phase angles: a reduction condition, necessary and algebraic, and a pressure-integrability condition, sufficient and differential. Separating them allows a failed construction to be located rather than merely recorded. Unlike the stream-function route on which earlier tri-periodic solutions rest, the framework is not confined to three dimensions, and does not presuppose the Beltrami property. For 3 <= n <= 8 we prove that unforced solutions exist at n=3 and n=4 and nowhere else. In three dimensions the admissible phases form exactly two families, mirror images distinguished by the sign of the helicity; these families are known, and we establish that the construction admits no others, settling a completeness question left open when they were found. In four dimensions integrability reduces a one-parameter curve to a single family, so the quarter-period offset is forced, not assumed. The obstructions divide by parity: arithmetic at n=5,7, where every admissible phase vector annihilates the field; differential at n=6,8, where the field survives but its convective term is not a gradient. Every obstructed dimension nevertheless carries an exact forced solution in closed form. These are not mere self-balancing: the phases are those at which strain and rotation are in exact pointwise balance, so that no pressure is generated at all. What obstructs the unforced problem becomes, in the forced problem, an exactly prescribable input.
tldr: A phase-angle framework is developed to construct and classify n-tuple-periodic solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, showing unforced solutions exist only for n=3 and n=4 with obstacles in higher dimensions.
motivation: The paper aims to generalize and complete the classical construction of tri-periodic Navier-Stokes solutions beyond three dimensions, without relying on the stream-function route or the Beltrami property.
method: The velocity field is written as a difference of two n-fold cyclic trigonometric products made divergence-free by a telescoping identity, reducing the problem to a necessary algebraic reduction condition on the phase angles and a sufficient differential pressure-integrability condition.
result: For 3 ≤ n ≤ 8 unforced solutions exist only at n=3 and n=4; the three-dimensional admissible phases form exactly two helicity-mirror families (proven complete), while obstructions divide by parity into arithmetic (n=5,7) and differential (n=6,8) types, with exact forced solutions existing in every obstructed dimension.
conclusion: All incompressible Navier-Stokes unforced n-tuple-periodic solutions for n up to 8 are classified, and the obstructions in higher dimensions become exactly prescribable inputs for forced problems.

title: Stability Of Closed Leaves Holomorphic Foliations Via Torsion Behavior Of Groups Of Germs
authors: Javier Rib\'{o}n
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider a compact leaf [MATH] of a holomorphic foliation [MATH] such that all the leaves of the restriction of [MATH] to some neighborhood [MATH] of [MATH] are closed in [MATH]. We show that there exists an invariant germ of analytic set [MATH] in a neighborhood of [MATH], of dimension higher than [MATH], consisting of compact leaves, such that the volume of the leaves in [MATH] is uniformly bounded by above. We also provide a globalization of this result if the ambient manifold is projective. In order to study closed leaves foliations, and via the holonomy representation, we introduce a new concept, of independent interest, for subgroups [MATH] of germs of holomorphic diffeomorphisms, the so called {\it torsion locus}. We show that it is non-trivial if [MATH] has finite orbits.
tldr: The paper studies the stability of closed leaves in holomorphic foliations via a new notion of 'torsion locus' for groups of germs of holomorphic diffeomorphisms.
motivation: Understanding when compact leaves of a holomorphic foliation persist in a neighborhood is a central question in the local theory of foliations and complex dynamics.
method: Using the holonomy representation, the author introduces the torsion locus for subgroups of germs of holomorphic diffeomorphisms and analyzes the analytic germ structure of neighboring closed leaves.
result: The author proves the existence of an invariant analytic germ of higher dimension consisting of compact leaves with uniformly bounded volume, and provides a globalization in the projective setting.
conclusion: The work establishes a geometric stability result for closed leaves and introduces a tool (the torsion locus) of independent interest in the study of holomorphic germ groups.

title: Projection Geometry And Relaxed Quasi-orthogonality For Inf-sup Stable Galerkin Methods
authors: Tsogtgerel Gantumur
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an elementary, coordinate-free proof that uniformly inf-sup stable nested Petrov-Galerkin methods on Hilbert spaces satisfy relaxed general quasi-orthogonality. More precisely, the accumulated squared Galerkin increments over any window of [MATH] consecutive levels are bounded by the squared error at the beginning of the window times [MATH], where [MATH], and both [MATH] and the constant prefactor depend explicitly only on a uniform bound for the Galerkin projections. The proof uses the Hilbert space angle between consecutive blocks of a uniformly bounded compatible projection chain, together with a dyadic decomposition and duality. It avoids matrix representations, wavelet bases, and LU-factorization. For symmetric indefinite problems, we relate the argument to the positive and negative spectral splittings of the Galerkin detail spaces and obtain a valid finite-window version of the sign-decomposition approach. We also construct a fixed self-adjoint involution and a fixed nested, uniformly inf-sup stable Galerkin sequence for which full general quasi-orthogonality fails. The same construction yields, for every [MATH], finite-support targets whose full-tail ratios grow at least like [MATH]. Thus uniform inf-sup stability guarantees sublinear finite-window quasi-orthogonality, whereas full quasi-orthogonality requires additional hierarchical information in general.
tldr: The paper gives a coordinate-free proof that uniformly inf-sup stable nested Petrov-Galerkin methods satisfy relaxed finite-window quasi-orthogonality, and constructs a counterexample showing full quasi-orthogonality fails in general.
motivation: Quasi-orthogonality is a key tool for proving convergence rates of adaptive and multilevel Galerkin methods, but existing derivations often rely on matrix representations, wavelet bases, or LU factorizations that obscure the underlying geometry.
method: The proof uses the Hilbert space angle between consecutive blocks of a uniformly bounded compatible projection chain, combined with a dyadic decomposition and duality arguments; for symmetric indefinite problems the argument is related to positive and negative spectral splittings of the Galerkin detail spaces.
result: Accumulated squared Galerkin increments over any window of M levels are bounded by a constant times the squared error at the window's start, with constants depending only on a uniform bound for the Galerkin projections; a fixed self-adjoint involution and nested stable Galerkin sequence are constructed for which full quasi-orthogonality fails, with full-tail ratios growing at least logarithmically.
conclusion: Uniform inf-sup stability guarantees sublinear finite-window quasi-orthogonality, but full quasi-orthogonality requires additional hierarchical information in general.

title: Symmetric Solution Of The Bellman Optimality Equation For Repeated Harmony Game
authors: Hisato Komatsu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In social dilemma games, additional rewards or punishments have been studied as means of promoting cooperation. Therefore, it is important to investigate the ideal situation, in which such an additional payoff would change the game. In this study, we investigated the symmetric solution of the Bellman optimality equation for a repeated harmony game. The calculations showed that three types of symmetric solutions exist. One of them corresponds to the trivial All-C strategy, and another to the Win-stay Lose-shift strategy of the prisoners dilemma game. The nontrivial behavior of the strategy corresponding to the last solution is also discussed in detail. In addition, we numerically investigated which strategy the agents actually learn by the reinforcement learning algorithm.
tldr: The paper derives three types of symmetric solutions to the Bellman optimality equation for a repeated harmony game and studies which strategies reinforcement-learning agents actually learn.
motivation: Additional rewards or punishments have been proposed to promote cooperation in social dilemma games, motivating an investigation of the idealized setting in which such payoffs would actually change the game.
method: The authors analytically solve the Bellman optimality equation for a repeated harmony game under a symmetric-solution ansatz, and numerically simulate reinforcement learning to see which strategies emerge.
result: Three symmetric solutions are found, corresponding to All-C, a Win-stay Lose-shift-like strategy, and a third nontrivial strategy whose behavior is analyzed in detail; numerical learning experiments reveal which one agents converge to.
conclusion: The repeated harmony game admits multiple symmetric optimal strategies, and the reinforcement-learning dynamics select among them in a nontrivial way, informing the design of incentives for cooperation.

title: Plug 'n' Pray: Agentic LLM-based Detection Of Potential Log File Exposures In Third-Party Content Management System Plugins
authors: Sebastian Neef
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Content Management Systems (CMS), such as WordPress, power a large share of the web (~58%), and their extensibility through third-party plugins is a major source of their popularity as well as of their attack surface. One high-impact weakness that remains understudied is log file exposure by CMS plugins, which create log files for debugging or other purposes. If these files are insufficiently secured, they can disclose sensitive information (e.g. credentials, personal data) which has led to website compromises in the past. In this work, we present an agentic, LLM-based framework that automatically detects potential log file exposures in plugins of the most popular CMS (WordPress). Our agent analyzes each plugin by performing static and dynamic analysis. We evaluated our approach on the 300 most-installed WordPress plugins (about 0.6% of all), which together account for over 250M active installations, i.e. 75% of all active installations in the official plugin ecosystem. We manually validated each finding, reproducing 79 of 81 findings from 62 plugins. We observed that several protective measures appear to be implemented that we classify as creation-control (e.g. manual log activation) and access-control (e.g. deny rules in .htaccess). However, we find that multi-layered protection is required, but not always present. From these results we derive a taxonomy of log file path and protection patterns and deduce a set of best practices for developers to securely handle them. Finally, our study corroborates that agentic LLMs are an useful tool for security analysis.
