conclusion: The proposed solver is efficient and accurate for biharmonic and triharmonic equations, high-wavenumber problems, Stokes flow, and plate bending, outperforming existing approaches in computational efficiency.

title: Master Equations For Mean Field Game Of Controls: A Unification Of Weak Solution Notions
authors: Mengzhen Li, Xintian Liu, Chenchen Mou, Zhen Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this manuscript, we study the master equation for mean field game of controls, assuming only that the data are Lipschitz continuous in the measure variable. Accordingly, we propose a weaker notion of solution called weak solutions for the master equation. We establish the global well-posedness of the master equation for such solution under the Lasry-Lions monotonicity and displacement [MATH]-monotonicity conditions, respectively. The arguments rely on the analysis of the associated Pontryagin forward-backward stochastic differential equation system, especially the stability in the measure variable. Finally, we review several existing notions of non-smooth solution from the literature, namely good solutions, weak viscosity solutions, Lipschitz solutions, monotone solutions, and examine their relationship with our weak solution. We show that under appropriate assumptions all of them are equivalent by their definitions, and thus our manuscript provides a unification of weak solution notions for the master equations derived from mean field game of controls.
tldr: The paper introduces a weak solution notion for master equations arising in mean field games of controls and shows it unifies several existing non-smooth solution concepts.
motivation: Master equations for mean field games of controls typically require smoothness in the measure variable, which is too restrictive; the authors aim to weaken these regularity assumptions and clarify the landscape of existing weak solution notions.
method: Assuming only Lipschitz continuity in the measure variable, they analyze the associated Pontryagin forward-backward stochastic differential equation system, establishing stability in the measure variable to prove global well-posedness of the weak solution.
result: Global well-posedness is obtained under Lasry-Lions monotonicity and displacement monotonicity conditions, and good solutions, weak viscosity solutions, Lipschitz solutions, and monotone solutions are shown to be equivalent to the proposed weak solution under suitable assumptions.
conclusion: The work provides a unifying framework for weak solution notions of master equations in mean field game of controls, clarifying their relationships and reducing them to a single consistent concept.

title: Bilinearity Preserving Algebraic Flux Correction
authors: Abhinav Jha Sarthak Sourav Dash
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Algebraic flux correction schemes for convection--diffusion--reaction equations rely on linearity preservation to avoid unnecessary artificial diffusion: the limiter is inactive whenever the discrete solution is affine. On quadrilateral and hexahedral meshes, this is insufficient, since the finite element space also contains bilinear functions that are reproduced exactly on axis-aligned meshes. We show that a mesh patch admits bilinearity preservation if and only if the central node lies in the convex hull of its neighbours after lifting each neighbour by the product of its coordinate differences, and we derive a sharp explicit value for the limiter parameter on such patches when the cell edges are parallel to the coordinate axes. We further characterize the meshes on which a mapped bilinear finite element space reproduces a bilinear function exactly, thereby establishing a fundamental limitation on what any limiter can achieve on general quadrilaterals. Numerical experiments confirm the theory: on axis-aligned grids, the proposed limiter reproduces a bilinear solution to the accuracy of the nonlinear iteration, whereas the linearity-preserving limiter does not. A sensitivity study shows that the parameter required for bilinearity preservation lies close to the upper end of the range for which the nonlinear problem can be solved by the fixed-point iteration considered here.
tldr: The paper introduces bilinearity-preserving limiters for algebraic flux correction schemes in convection–diffusion–reaction problems on quadrilateral and hexahedral meshes, characterizing when a mesh patch admits exact reproduction of bilinear functions.
motivation: Standard linearity-preserving limiters fail to avoid unnecessary artificial diffusion on quadrilateral/hexahedral meshes, because the finite element space contains bilinear functions reproduced exactly on axis-aligned meshes.
method: The authors derive a geometric necessary-and-sufficient condition for bilinearity preservation based on the central node lying in a lifted convex hull of its neighbours, obtain a sharp explicit limiter parameter for axis-parallel cells, and characterize meshes where mapped bilinear spaces reproduce bilinear functions.
result: Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed limiter reproduces bilinear solutions to nonlinear-iteration accuracy on axis-aligned grids, while linearity-preserving limiters do not; a sensitivity study bounds the admissible parameter range for fixed-point convergence.
conclusion: Bilinearity preservation is achievable on specific mesh families, and a fundamental limitation on any limiter for general quadrilaterals is established, guiding practical limiter design in flux-corrected finite element schemes.

title: Teaching Vampire New Tricks: An Experimental Study Of Neural Clause Selection
authors: Karel Chvalovsk\'y, Martin Suda, Josef Urban
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A neural clause-selection guidance approach in the Vampire theorem prover was recently shown to substantially improve the success rate of the prover's default strategy on the TPTP benchmark. We experimentally study the impact of the approach across several ITP-derived benchmark sets and its interaction with theorem proving strategies. We find that while the neural guidance consistently improves performance within individual benchmark domains, cross-benchmark application of guiding models underperforms the plain default strategy. This can be remedied by training a single model on all datasets at once. Such a model, although more expensive to obtain, helps Vampire almost catch up in performance across all datasets. The picture when considering combined strategies is less clear-cut, indicating persisting value of neural guidance but under diminishing returns.
tldr: An experimental study of neural clause-selection guidance in the Vampire automated theorem prover across ITP-derived benchmarks.
motivation: Neural clause selection was previously shown to improve Vampire's default strategy on TPTP, but its generalization across benchmark domains and interaction with proving strategies was unclear.
method: The authors evaluate a neural clause-selection guidance model on several ITP-derived benchmark sets, testing cross-benchmark application of guiding models versus training a single model on all datasets, and examine combined strategies.
result: Neural guidance consistently helps within individual domains, but cross-benchmark transfer underperforms the plain default; a single jointly trained model nearly recovers performance across all datasets.
conclusion: Neural clause selection retains value but shows diminishing returns, and multi-dataset training is needed for robust cross-domain gains.

title: Illusion Of Depth: Revealing Hidden Stereo Vision Vulnerabilities In Depth Estimation
authors: Sri Hrushikesh Varma Bhupathiraju, Tetsu Ishizue, Nicholas U. Costagliola, Ozora Sako, Kentaro Yoshioka, Takeshi Sugawara, Sara Rampazzi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stereo cameras are integrated into autonomous systems such as self-driving cars, drones, and robots to offer precise depth estimation in a cost-effective manner compared to LiDAR technology. In this work, we reveal an intrinsic vulnerability in stereo cameras that stems from their pixel sampling and calibration processes, which can influence the outputs of stereo matching algorithms. Attackers can achieve fine-grained control over the estimated depth of real obstacles using simple repeating patterns, without relying on sophisticated adversarial machine learning techniques. Furthermore, deep learning-based depth estimation models exhibit a similar vulnerability. We evaluate the impact of this attack on two widely used stereo matching algorithms (BM and SGBM), three deep learning models (PSMNet, MoCha-Stereo, and UniMatch), a stereo-LiDAR fusion model (SGM-DDC), and two popular commercial stereo cameras, the ZED2 and Intel RealSense D435. For example, in the ZED2 camera, an attacker can displace obstacles up to 20~meters farther or 12~meters closer. In our real-world evaluation in a driving setting, a brief 0.5~second attack can trigger emergency braking in a popular autonomous driving framework. We further demonstrate the feasibility at driving speeds up to 40~km/h using CARLA. Finally, we confirm the ineffectiveness of state-of-the-art defenses, and we propose a novel strategy that leverages similarity scores to dynamically detect and suppress the depth discrepancies. Our work highlights vulnerabilities hidden in stereo matching and deep learning depth estimation models, addressing critical limitations in autonomous system deployments.
tldr: The paper uncovers an intrinsic vulnerability in stereo camera depth estimation, where simple repeating patterns can finely control the estimated depth of obstacles in both classical and deep-learning stereo matching pipelines.
motivation: Stereo cameras are widely deployed in autonomous systems for cost-effective depth estimation, but their pixel sampling and calibration processes may hide exploitable weaknesses that could compromise safety-critical perception.
method: The authors exploit pixel sampling and calibration artifacts to design repeating-pattern attacks, then evaluate them against two classical stereo matching algorithms (BM, SGBM), three deep learning models (PSMNet, MoCha-Stereo, UniMatch), a stereo-LiDAR fusion model, and commercial cameras (ZED2, Intel RealSense D435), including real-world driving and CARLA simulations.
result: Attacks displace obstacles by up to 20 m farther or 12 m closer in the ZED2, and a 0.5-second attack triggered emergency braking in an autonomous driving framework; state-of-the-art defenses proved ineffective at up to 40 km/h driving speeds.
conclusion: The work exposes critical depth-estimation vulnerabilities in deployed stereo and learning-based perception systems, and proposes a similarity-score-based detection and suppression strategy as a mitigation.

title: Auction Design With ROI-Constrained Bidders: Truthfulness And Revenue Maximization
authors: Zhiqiang Zhuang, Quan Yu, Yisong Wang, Kewen Wang, Zhe Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The return-on-investment (ROI) constraint is central to many auctions, particularly in online advertising, where a bidder is unwilling to pay more than a fixed fraction of the value obtained. We study truthful and revenue-maximizing auctions for ROI-constrained bidders. We first characterize truthful auctions when both valuations and ROI constraints are private, showing that the allocation rule uniquely determines the payment rule. Building on this characterization, for multiple bidders we introduce [MATH]-increment mechanisms that resemble Myerson's optimal mechanism~; as [MATH] vanishes, these mechanisms become asymptotically optimal among deterministic truthful mechanisms, and their revenue approaches at least a [MATH] fraction of the optimal expected revenue over all truthful mechanisms, where [MATH] is the largest possible ROI constraint. In the single-bidder setting, we prove that every truthful auction can be replaced by a convex pricing function with weakly higher payments for every type, and we derive the optimal pricing functions when either the valuation or the ROI constraint is public.
tldr: The paper studies truthful and revenue-maximizing auction design when bidders have private return-on-investment (ROI) constraints.
motivation: ROI constraints are central in online advertising and other auction settings where bidders limit payment to a fraction of value obtained, but existing auction theory largely ignores them.
method: It characterizes truthful auctions with private valuations and ROI constraints, introduces increment mechanisms analogous to Myerson's optimal mechanism, and analyzes convex pricing functions in the single-bidder setting.
result: The allocation rule uniquely determines payments, the proposed mechanisms are asymptotically optimal as the ROI increment vanishes and guarantee at least a fraction of optimal expected revenue, and optimal pricing functions are derived for public valuation or public ROI.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for designing truthful, revenue-maximizing auctions under ROI constraints, bridging mechanism design and practical advertising auctions.

title: A Cyber Range Evaluation Of Autonomous Network Incident Response Agents
authors: Jakob Nyberg, Teodor Sommestad, Andrei Buhaiu, Joakim Loxdal, Pontus Johnson, Mathias Ekstedt
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We test the performance of agents for automated network intrusion response in a cyber range intended for human operator training. The range implements an emulated networking environment with a variable network topology, red-team emulation and simulated user agents. The goal of the defensive agents is to prevent hosts in the network from being accessed by the red-team agent, while minimizing the availability costs induced from defensive measures. Alerts are generated using a SIEM platform and mapped to a data modeling language used by the agents. We test a combination of heuristic agents and policies learned using reinforcement learning. The learned policies are optimized to minimize the combined cost using a cyber attack simulator modeling the network. We found that the reinforcement learning agents were overall more efficient at defending the system than the heuristic policy, and that the performance depends highly on the policy of the adversary in combination with the simulated users.
tldr: The paper evaluates heuristic and reinforcement-learning agents for autonomous network intrusion response inside a cyber range originally built for human operator training.
motivation: Automating defensive responses to network intrusions could reduce operator workload and reaction time, but the relative effectiveness of learned versus hand-crafted defense policies is unclear.
method: A cyber range with emulated variable network topologies, red-team emulation, and simulated user agents generates SIEM alerts mapped into a data modeling language; heuristic agents and RL-trained policies are compared, with the learned policies optimized in a cyber attack simulator.
result: Reinforcement-learning agents defended the network more efficiently overall than the heuristic policy, and their performance depended strongly on the adversary's policy and the behavior of simulated users.
conclusion: Learned policies show promise for automated incident response, but robustness depends on modeling of adversaries and users, motivating further work on evaluation realism.

title: GPUThor: Amplifying Rowhammer Attacks Via Non-Uniform Patterns To Exploit ECC-Protected GPUs
authors: Chris S. Lin, Joyce Qu, Aditya Rajeev, Gururaj Saileshwar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GDDR memory in GPUs is vulnerable to Rowhammer attacks, where rapid memory accesses induce bit flips in adjacent cells, enabling data tampering and privilege escalation. However, prior GPU Rowhammer attacks trigger only tens to hundreds of bit flips, orders of magnitude fewer than CPU attacks, severely limiting their practical impact. This gap stems from the reliance of existing GPU Rowhammer attacks on uniform hammering patterns that activate aggressor and decoy rows equally, which results in low hammering intensity for aggressor rows. We present GPUThor, a high-intensity Rowhammer attack on NVIDIA GPUs leveraging non-uniform hammering. GPUThor reverse engineers GPU memory-access coalescing behavior to enable non-uniform hammering patterns on GPUs, that activate aggressor rows more intensely than decoy rows. Additionally, by identifying refresh instances when in-DRAM mitigations are applied, it constructs longer attack patterns that escape mitigation across refresh intervals, further increasing hammering intensity. Together, these techniques yield 500X to 23,500X more bit flips than prior GPU Rowhammer attacks, across several NVIDIA GPUs (A4000, A4500, A5000, A6000), reaching bit flip rates close to state-of-the-art CPU Rowhammer attacks. GPUThor also enables the first Rowhammer exploits on ECC-protected GPUs, inducing uncorrectable double and triple bit flips, making denial-of-service and privilege-escalation attacks practical even on GPUs with ECC enabled.
tldr: GPUThor is a high-intensity Rowhammer attack on NVIDIA GPUs that uses non-uniform hammering patterns to increase bit-flip rates by 500x–23,500x and enable the first exploits on ECC-protected GPUs.
motivation: Existing GPU Rowhammer attacks rely on uniform hammering patterns that activate aggressor and decoy rows equally, producing only tens to hundreds of bit flips—orders of magnitude fewer than CPU attacks—which limits their practical impact.
method: The authors reverse engineer GPU memory-access coalescing to construct non-uniform hammering patterns that intensify aggressor-row activation, and identify refresh instances when in-DRAM mitigations are applied to build longer attack patterns that evade mitigation across refresh intervals.
result: The attack yields 500x–23,500x more bit flips than prior GPU Rowhammer work across NVIDIA A4000, A4500, A5000, and A6000 GPUs, reaching rates near state-of-the-art CPU attacks, and induces uncorrectable double/triple bit flips on ECC-protected GPUs.
conclusion: GPUThor makes denial-of-service and privilege-escalation Rowhammer attacks practical even on ECC-protected GPUs, showing that GDDR memory is far more vulnerable than previously demonstrated.

title: When Agents See Differently: Exposing Ui Desynchronization Threats In Mobile Agents
authors: Heng Li, Fulin Zhao, Zhe Geng, Zhiyuan Yao, Wei Yuan, Xiapu Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobile agents are increasingly capable of autonomously interacting with mobile applications and performing consequential actions on behalf of users. Effective human oversight of such agents relies on a basic premise: users and agents observe consistent information from the same interface. We show that this premise can be systematically violated. Users perceive mobile interfaces through physical displays and the human visual system, making their observations subject to occlusion and luminance contrast limitations. In contrast, agents consume digital screenshots that may retain such content and accessibility representations that expose nonvisual widget metadata. The same UI state can therefore present materially different information to users and agents, a mismatch we term human-agent UI desynchronization. We investigate whether a repackaged clone of a legitimate APK can exploit this desynchronization to steer an agent toward attacker-designated actions, while remaining fully functional and behaviorally consistent with the original application for human users. We demonstrate that this threat is feasible: perturbations embedded before deployment can induce such deviations without access to runtime user instructions, agent detection or online adaptation. To systematically expose and evaluate this threat, we develop an automated framework that constructs user runtime instruction-agnostic UI desynchronization attacks and realizes them in deployable APKs. We conduct static and dynamic evaluations across five mobile-agent frameworks and three backbone models on 546 tasks involving various applications, achieving average misleading rates of 77.9% and 66.9%, respectively. A complementary questionnaire-based study with 186 participants finds that the visual perturbations used in our attacks are difficult for human users to notice.
tldr: The paper exposes a security threat in mobile agents where attackers can craft repackaged APKs that present different UI information to human users versus automated agents, steering agents toward attacker-chosen actions.
motivation: Human oversight of autonomous mobile agents assumes users and agents perceive the same interface, but users rely on physical displays (subject to occlusion and luminance limits) while agents consume screenshots and accessibility metadata, which may differ.
method: The authors build an automated framework that generates user-instruction-agnostic UI desynchronization attacks and realizes them in deployable APKs, evaluated statically and dynamically across five mobile-agent frameworks and three backbone models on 546 tasks.
result: Attacks achieve average misleading rates of 77.9% (static) and 66.9% (dynamic), while a questionnaire study with 186 participants shows the visual perturbations are difficult for humans to notice.
conclusion: Human-agent UI desynchronization is a feasible and previously unrecognized attack surface for mobile agents, calling for defenses that ensure consistent perception between users and agents.

title: Qualitative Properties And Stability Analysis Of Autonomous And Non-Autonomous Longitudinal T2dm Models
authors: V. E. S. Szab\'o
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the qualitative properties, long-term dynamic behavior, and stability of a longitudinal mathematical model describing the progression of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). We significantly extend and refine the mathematical analysis of the model recently proposed by De Gaetano et al. (Journal of Theoretical Biology, 2024). Specifically, we analyze both the autonomous system with a fixed age parameter and the non-autonomous system incorporating explicit time-dependent aging dynamics under generalized conditions, providing rigorous proofs for global existence, uniqueness, positivity, asymptotic bounds, and stability properties.
tldr: The paper provides rigorous mathematical analysis of autonomous and non-autonomous longitudinal models of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus progression, proving global existence, uniqueness, positivity, asymptotic bounds, and stability.
motivation: The model recently proposed by De Gaetano et al. (2024) describes T2DM progression but lacks a fully rigorous qualitative and stability analysis, particularly when age-dependent (non-autonomous) dynamics are included.
method: Dynamical systems and ODE analysis are applied to both a fixed-age autonomous system and a time-dependent non-autonomous aging system, establishing proofs of well-posedness, positivity, boundedness, and stability.
result: The authors establish global existence, uniqueness, positivity, asymptotic bounds, and stability properties for both the autonomous and non-autonomous T2DM models under generalized conditions.
conclusion: The refined analysis extends and strengthens the mathematical foundation of longitudinal T2DM modeling, though it lies entirely outside quantum information science and its associated research directions.

title: Asymmetric Weighted Earliness-Tardiness: Scheduling With A Nonrestrictive Common Due Date
authors: Nicholas G. Hall (the Ohio State University), Hans Kellerer (university Of Graz, Austria), Miao Song
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-machine asymmetric weighted earliness--tardiness (AWET) scheduling asks how to sequence jobs around a common synchronization date when early and late completion incur unrelated job-dependent penalties. At the boundary nonrestrictive date [MATH], a compact V-shaped schedule reduces the continuous-time problem to a quadratic choice of a nonempty early set. We establish four complementary results for this model. First, the positive-integer problem is strongly NP-complete by a unary-polynomial reduction from Restricted Exact Cover by 3-Sets. Second, unrestricted AWET admits a polynomial-time [MATH]-approximation based on an anchored semidefinite relaxation and deterministic marginal thresholding. Third, when the earliness and tardiness ratio orders are strict reversals, the problem is weakly NP-complete but has an exact two-resource pseudopolynomial dynamic program. Fourth, for fixed total refinements whose ratio permutation is separable, an exact separating-tree recurrence and coordinated geometric trimming yield an FPTAS. The proofs use different manifestations of the same canonical objective: scale-separated prefix penalties, positive-semidefinite minimum-kernel covariance, a dominant completed load square, and a bounded four-coordinate decomposition interface. Together, the results show that the decisive issue is not merely whether the two ratio orders agree, but whether their interaction can be controlled by a global certificate or compressed into a bounded constructive interface.
tldr: This paper studies single-machine asymmetric weighted earliness-tardiness scheduling with a nonrestrictive common due date, establishing complexity results, approximation guarantees, and an FPTAS.
motivation: Scheduling jobs around a common synchronization date with job-dependent early and late penalties models just-in-time production, but the asymmetric weighted variant lacks a complete complexity and algorithmic characterization.
method: The authors exploit a V-shaped schedule structure to reduce the continuous-time problem to a quadratic choice of an early set, then apply reductions from Restricted Exact Cover by 3-Sets, an anchored semidefinite relaxation with marginal thresholding, a pseudopolynomial dynamic program, and a separating-tree recurrence with geometric trimming.
result: The problem is shown to be strongly NP-complete in general, admits a polynomial-time approximation, is only weakly NP-complete under reversed ratio orders with an exact pseudopolynomial DP, and yields an FPTAS for separable ratio permutations.
conclusion: The decisive factor is not simply whether the two ratio orders agree, but whether their interaction can be controlled by a global certificate or compressed into a bounded constructive interface.

title: Largest Circle Enclosing Exactly $n$ Interior Lattice Points. Ii
authors: Jianqiang Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a previous article doi.org/10.3390/geometry2030012, the author investigated a class of elementary plane geometry problems closely related to the theme of this work. Here, we prove a weaker version of a previous conjecture by demonstrating that there are infinitely many maximally circlable (MAC) numbers -- positive integers [MATH] for which there exists a largest circle enclosing exactly [MATH] interior lattice points. Furthermore, by extending numerical computations to [MATH], we identify two counterexamples to a conjecture in loc cit. regarding the symmetry of the largest circle enclosing a strong MAC number (a MAC number [MATH] where [MATH] is non-MAC). We also propose a potential infinite family of strong MAC numbers derived from Pythagorean triples; the existence of this family would imply the infinity of non-MAC numbers, as conjectured by Zhao. Throughout this paper, we provide extensive data characterizing both MAC and strong MAC numbers alongside their corresponding largest enclosing circles.
tldr: The paper proves a weaker version of a conjecture about 'maximally circlable' (MAC) numbers—positive integers n for which a largest circle encloses exactly n interior lattice points—showing infinitely many such numbers exist and identifying counterexamples to a symmetry conjecture.
motivation: The work continues prior research on elementary plane geometry problems concerning circles enclosing lattice points, aiming to resolve conjectures about the infinitude and symmetry properties of MAC numbers.
method: The author provides a mathematical proof of the infinitude of MAC numbers, extends numerical computations up to a large bound to test conjectures, and proposes a potential infinite family of 'strong MAC' numbers derived from Pythagorean triples.
result: Infinitely many MAC numbers are shown to exist (a weaker form of the original conjecture), two counterexamples to the symmetry conjecture for strong MAC numbers are found, and extensive computational data characterizing MAC and strong MAC numbers is provided.
conclusion: The findings support the conjecture that non-MAC numbers are infinite (via the proposed Pythagorean-triple family) and clarify the structure of maximal enclosing circles, while leaving the full original conjecture open.

title: GPU-Accelerated Presolving For Linear Programming
authors: Stephen Boyd Daniel Cederberg
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent research has focused on developing GPU-accelerated algorithms for solving linear programs (LPs), with results that are nothing short of extraordinary. But a complete solver pipeline consists of more than the core algorithm, and the elephant in the room is that stages such as presolve have remained on the CPU, where they have become an increasingly large bottleneck. Presolve has stayed on the CPU because of the longstanding view, held by academic and industrial developers alike, that it is inherently sequential and irregular, and therefore difficult to parallelize efficiently. In this paper we challenge this view and show that presolving can benefit substantially from GPU acceleration. We describe simple design principles that avoid severe load imbalance and expose parallelism in reductions that appear inherently sequential. We implement these principles in cuPSLP, a GPU-accelerated version of PSLP, a CPU-based presolver that is itself several times faster than a state-of-the-art commercial presolver. In our experiments, cuPSLP reduces the shifted geometric mean presolve time of PSLP by a factor of 11 on the Mittelmann LP benchmark set and 42 on the GAMS large-scale LP benchmark set, with similar reduction quality.
tldr: The paper presents cuPSLP, a GPU-accelerated presolver for linear programming that substantially reduces presolve time compared to CPU-based PSLP.
motivation: Presolve stages in LP solvers have remained CPU-bound and are becoming a bottleneck as core LP algorithms are accelerated on GPUs.
method: The authors design GPU-friendly presolve algorithms that avoid load imbalance and expose parallelism in reductions traditionally viewed as sequential, implementing them in cuPSLP.
result: cuPSLP reduces the shifted geometric mean presolve time of PSLP by a factor of 11 on the Mittelmann LP benchmark set and 42 on the GAMS large-scale LP benchmark set, with similar reduction quality.
conclusion: GPU acceleration can substantially benefit LP presolving, challenging the view that presolve is inherently sequential and unsuitable for parallelization.

title: Dimensional Decomposition And Column Generation For Bin Dimensioning In E-Commerce Fulfillment Centers
authors: Mari\'a C. V. Nascimento Gabriel Gonz\'alez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fulfillment center (FC) is a specialized logistics facility where e-commerce inventory is received, stored, and processed. Its internal organization directly impacts space utilization and the performance of put-away and picking operations. Items are stored in bins following strict operational guidelines to ensure productivity in both activities, so bin dimensions must be tailored to the product profile of each facility to maximize space utilization. % We address the bin dimensioning problem arising in e-commerce fulfillment centers: given a set of candidate bin types and a large, heterogeneous inventory, determine the number of bins of each type and assign all items so as to minimize total bin volume, subject to operational constraints governing how products may be combined within a single bin. We develop a dimensional decomposition that exploits these constraints to reduce the three-dimensional packing problem to a one-dimensional block-positioning problem. Building on this decomposition, we formulate the problem as a mixed-integer linear program and propose two solution methods: a Best-Fit-Decreasing (BFD) heuristic and a column generation scheme that produces tight LP lower bounds. Computational experiments on four synthetic datasets, calibrated on proprietary data from an American e-commerce fintech and ranging from 1.5 thousand to 1.5 million SKUs, show that the BFD heuristic scales to instances with up to 1.7 million blocks, and that column generation certifies a BFD--LP gap of 2.26\% on the smallest dataset. The experiments further reveal a structural divide in solution quality across datasets, driven by the interaction between operational constraints and each facility's product profile.
tldr: The paper develops a dimensional decomposition and column generation approach to solve a bin dimensioning problem in e-commerce fulfillment centers, minimizing total bin volume subject to operational packing constraints.
motivation: Fulfillment centers must tailor bin dimensions to heterogeneous product profiles to maximize space utilization, but the resulting assignment and dimensioning problem is a large-scale combinatorial optimization challenge.
method: The authors exploit operational constraints to reduce a three-dimensional packing problem to a one-dimensional block-positioning problem, formulate it as a mixed-integer linear program, and propose a Best-Fit-Decreasing heuristic plus a column generation scheme yielding tight LP lower bounds.
result: Experiments on four synthetic datasets (1.5 thousand to 1.5 million SKUs) show the BFD heuristic scales to 1.7 million blocks, while column generation certifies a 2.26% BFD-LP gap on the smallest dataset.
conclusion: The decomposition enables scalable solutions, though a structural divide in solution quality emerges depending on the interaction between operational constraints and facility product profiles.

title: The Exact Dimensional Threshold For Spearman Rank-correlation Compatibility
authors: Zhenyuan Zhang Ruodu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, for a given dimension, the set of Spearman's rank correlation matrices and that of linear correlation matrices coincide if and only if the dimension is no larger than nine. For this, we construct an extreme rank-four counterexample in dimension ten and prove its incompatibility using moment identities and Cauchy-Schwarz. Appending unit directions produces counterexamples in every higher dimension. This, together with existing results, completes the dimensional classification and settles a long-standing open question in quantitative risk management.
tldr: The paper determines the exact dimension threshold (nine) at which Spearman rank correlation matrices cease to coincide with linear correlation matrices, settling a long-standing open problem in quantitative risk management.
motivation: Understanding when rank correlations can be represented as linear correlations is fundamental for dependence modeling in risk management, where Spearman's rho is widely used but lacks a complete compatibility characterization.
method: The authors construct an extreme rank-four counterexample in dimension ten and prove its incompatibility using moment identities and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities, then extend it to all higher dimensions by appending unit directions.
result: For dimension ≤ 9 the two sets of correlation matrices coincide, but in dimension 10 they differ, and the same incompatibility persists in every higher dimension, completing the dimensional classification.
conclusion: The exact dimensional threshold is nine, resolving a long-standing question and providing a definitive theoretical boundary for the use of Spearman rank correlations in multivariate dependence modeling.

title: A Heterogeneous FitzHugh-Nagumo Model Exhibiting Local And Regional Dynamics That Mimic Spontaneous Atrial Fibrillation
authors: Alexander Hattoum, Camden Kilton, Martin Mohlenkamp, Graham Walther, Qiliang Wu, Todd Young
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two-dimensional networks of FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators in regimes that mimic cardiac tissue. The networks include small layers of cells that have fast-recovery characteristics and adjacent layers of cells that have slow-recovery. Numerical simulations show that the boundary between the fast- and slow-recovery cells can initiate fibrillatory-like behavior when activated by a single, healthy wave in the network. We discuss possible connections between these structures and the onset of atrial fibrillation, with the goal of improving our understanding and treatment of this costly condition. Our main conclusion is that a single, normal excitation of small areas of heterogeneity embedded in healthy tissue can initiate arrhythmias and the two dimensional network can then sustain irregular firing patterns in the form of double swirling-back curves and spiral waves. This occurs with a very simple model of excitable cells and we give a clear mechanistic description of the arrhythmia. The model illustrates how increasing heterogeneity in heart tissue can progressively cause first intermittent and then persistent arrhythmic behavior. Another conclusion is that the center of problematic firings can drift away from the heterogeneity into healthy tissue, thus presenting phantom targets for treatment.
tldr: A heterogeneous two-dimensional FitzHugh-Nagumo network is shown to initiate and sustain spiral-wave dynamics that mimic spontaneous atrial fibrillation.
motivation: The authors aim to better understand the onset and maintenance of atrial fibrillation by using a minimal model of excitable cells with fast- and slow-recovery heterogeneity.
method: They simulate two-dimensional networks of FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators composed of adjacent layers with fast-recovery and slow-recovery characteristics and analyze wave initiation and spiral-wave behavior.
result: A single healthy wave activating the boundary between heterogeneous regions can trigger fibrillatory-like irregular firing, sustained by double swirling-back curves and spiral waves that may drift into healthy tissue.
conclusion: The model provides a mechanistic explanation for how increasing tissue heterogeneity can cause intermittent then persistent arrhythmias, suggesting phantom targets for treatment.

title: Stability Analysis Of Generalized Multi-Source Weber Problems
authors: N. H. Hai, V. S. T. Long, N. M. Nam, N. D. Yen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a stability analysis of the generalized multi-source Weber problems under the influence of data perturbation within the framework of the Minkowski function. First, we establish explicit Lipschitz constants for the objective functions and optimal value functions. Then, we prove several properties of the global optimal solution sets. Furthermore, we provide sufficient conditions for the upper semicontinuity of global solution mappings and the inner semicontinuity of local solution mappings. Three illustrative examples are constructed. Our results give indirect answers to several open questions regarding the stability of local optimal solution mappings of the optimization problems discussed.
tldr: This paper analyzes the stability of generalized multi-source Weber location problems under data perturbations using Minkowski functionals.
motivation: Multi-source Weber problems are classical facility-location optimization models, and understanding how their optimal values and solution sets behave under data perturbation is important for robust decision-making.
method: The authors derive explicit Lipschitz constants for objective functions and optimal value functions, then establish properties of global optimal solution sets and continuity conditions for global and local solution mappings.
result: Sufficient conditions are given for upper semicontinuity of global solution mappings and inner semicontinuity of local solution mappings, illustrated with three examples.
conclusion: The results indirectly answer several open questions about the stability of local optimal solution mappings in these optimization problems.

title: Subspaces Of $l^1$ Spanned By The Even And Odd Levels Of The Haar System
authors: Thomas Speckhofer
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the closed subspace of [MATH] spanned by the even (respectively, odd) levels of the Haar system is not isomorphic to [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that the closed subspaces of l1 spanned by the even and odd levels of the Haar system are not isomorphic to l1.
motivation: The Haar system is a classical basis in Banach space theory, and understanding the isomorphic structure of its level subspaces in l1 addresses a natural question in functional analysis.
method: The author uses Banach space techniques and properties of the Haar system to analyze the closed linear spans of even and odd levels within l1.
result: It is shown that neither the even-level nor the odd-level subspace is isomorphic to the full space l1.
conclusion: These subspaces exhibit a distinct isomorphic type, contributing to the structural theory of l1 and its subspaces.

title: Exploiting And Securing Docker Containers And Kubernetes Pods From A MitM Attack
authors: Henry Kabuye, Ismail Khalid Kazmi, Chunyan Mu, Paolo Modesti
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: PURPOSE - Workloads in containers, such as Docker containers and Kubernetes pods, are vulnerable to many of the same attacks as workloads in non-container environments, including phishing, application exploits and network intrusions. This systematic review and design-and-creation study explores techniques for securing containerised-based operating systems against Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks. The proposed framework uses a conceptual model for representing communication and cryptographic primitives, together with the AnBxJ Java security library and container firewalls operating at layer 7 of the OSI model. The study addresses the question: How can containerised-based operating systems be effectively secured from Man-in-the-Middle attacks? It aims to support practitioners in protecting Docker and Kubernetes deployments by systematising security practices and applying a zero trust architecture. METHODOLOGY - The research uses a Systematic Review (SR) based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA), bringing together evidence from studies addressing the same research topic. FINDINGS - Success factors were identified, and a security mechanism was successfully implemented in a containerised-based operating system scenario. VALUE - The findings may help practitioners protect Kubernetes and Docker installations by systematising container security practices and providing a zero trust architecture for containerised-based operating systems.
tldr: A systematic review and design framework for securing Docker containers and Kubernetes pods against Man-in-the-Middle attacks using a zero trust architecture and layer-7 firewalls.
motivation: Containerised workloads are vulnerable to MitM attacks, and practitioners need systematised security practices for Docker and Kubernetes deployments.
method: Systematic review following PRISMA guidelines, combined with a design-and-creation study using a conceptual model, the AnBxJ Java security library, and container firewalls at OSI layer 7.
result: Success factors were identified and a security mechanism was implemented in a containerised-based operating system scenario.
conclusion: The proposed zero trust architecture and systematised security practices can help protect Kubernetes and Docker installations from MitM attacks.

title: Vibe-Coded And Tuned: A State-of-the-Art Smt Solver For Qf-lra
authors: Jan Jakub\r{u}v Mikol\'a\v{s} Janota
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents the SMT solver primo, which is fully vibe-coded and then parameter-tuned, achieving state-of-the-art results on linear real arithmetic (QF-LRA). The performance of primo is achieved by a systematic literature survey, repeated profiling, and parameter tuning. The resulting solver outperforms the winner of the QF-LRA track of SMT-COMP~2026. This confirms that vibe-coding of automated reasoning tools will enable us to make great strides in the future.
tldr: The paper introduces primo, a fully vibe-coded and parameter-tuned SMT solver that achieves state-of-the-art performance on the QF-LRA (quantifier-free linear real arithmetic) benchmark track.
motivation: The authors aim to show that LLM-assisted ('vibe') coding combined with systematic literature survey, profiling, and parameter tuning can produce competitive automated reasoning tools, potentially accelerating development in the field.
method: They conducted a systematic literature survey of existing SMT techniques, implemented the solver via vibe-coding, and iteratively profiled and tuned its parameters to optimize performance on QF-LRA instances.
result: The resulting solver outperforms the winner of the QF-LRA track of SMT-COMP 2026, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on that benchmark class.
conclusion: The authors conclude that vibe-coding of automated reasoning tools will enable rapid future progress in solver development.

title: InceptionRAG: Stealthy Poisoning Attack Against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jiachang Zhang, Min Chen, Xiao Ren, Zhenyong Zhang, Yuanchao Shu, Yunjun Gao, Zhikun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems enhance large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge but have been demonstrated to be vulnerable to corpus poisoning. Existing poisoning attacks against RAG largely focus on single-point explicit injection, where the malicious payload is fully encapsulated within a single document. Consequently, recent mitigation mechanisms have evolved to identify and diminish these threats effectively. In this paper, we first verify that existing mitigation mechanisms are insufficient for a new class of threats: indirect logic induction. Motivated by this observation, we introduce InceptionRAG, a stealthy attack mechanism that subverts the standard attack paradigm. Instead of injecting explicit malicious payloads, InceptionRAG fragments it into a chain of dormant passages. These passages appear harmless and can bypass existing mitigation mechanisms when examined separately. However, when retrieved together, they trigger LLMs to self-deduce target misinformation via multi-hop reasoning. To further improve the applicability of InceptionRAG in black-box settings, we propose zeroth-order suffix optimization (ZOSO) to automate the generation of authoritative suffixes. Extensive evaluations across three datasets and three LLMs demonstrate that InceptionRAG achieves an attack success rate exceeding 80% even under rigorous adversarial constraints. In particular, InceptionRAG shows superior evasion capabilities, effectively bypassing established defenses that mitigate traditional single-document injections. Our findings expose a concerning paradox: the stronger reasoning capabilities of LLMs increase their vulnerability to reasoning-based poisoning attacks. To mitigate potential misuse, we propose a document isolation-based defense, HODOR, which decouples adversarial logical dependencies.
tldr: InceptionRAG is a stealthy poisoning attack that fragments malicious payloads into dormant passages, which trigger misinformation via multi-hop reasoning in RAG systems.
motivation: Existing RAG poisoning attacks use single-point explicit injection and are increasingly mitigated; the authors identify indirect logic induction as a new threat class that bypasses current defenses.
method: The attack splits a malicious payload into benign-looking passages that together induce LLMs to self-deduce target misinformation; zeroth-order suffix optimization (ZOSO) automates authoritative suffix generation for black-box settings.
result: InceptionRAG achieves over 80% attack success rate across three datasets and three LLMs, effectively evading established defenses that mitigate traditional single-document injections.
conclusion: The paper exposes a paradox where stronger LLM reasoning increases vulnerability to reasoning-based poisoning attacks, and proposes a document isolation defense, HODOR, to decouple adversarial logical dependencies.

title: Direct Observation Of Dipolar-Driven Anisotropic Quantum Projection Noise In A Solid-State Spin Ensemble
authors: Tasuku Ono, Weijie Wu, Haopu Yang, Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, Benjamin Brenner, Che Liu, Collin Fan, Chris R. Laumann, Jonathan N. Hall\'en, Emily J. Davis, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, Norman Y. Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond is a prominent quantum-sensing platform. Combining readout at the quantum projection noise limit with strong dipolar interactions promises substantial gains in sensitivity. However, experimentally accessing this regime has remained a longstanding challenge. In this work, we demonstrate quantum-projection-noise-resolved readout of a strongly-interacting, two-dimensional ensemble of NV centers. Our approach leverages repetitive readout via the NV's intrinsic [MATH]N nuclear memory at a moderate magnetic field ([MATH] T), improving the readout fidelities by nearly an order of magnitude. This enables us to directly resolve the quantum projection noise of a coherent spin state and to watch the ensemble's intrinsic dipolar interactions shear this noise into an anisotropic profile. Our results open the door to direct measurements of spin squeezing and entanglement-enhanced sensing in the solid state.

title: Designs Without Disorder: Unitary $k$-designs From A Single-site Bulk Defect
authors: Pratik Nandy Samudra Sur
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that an [MATH] local defect is sufficient to generate approximate unitary [MATH]-designs from an otherwise integrable quantum many-body system. Using a two-Pauli-kick (2PK) protocol with temporal sampling, we demonstrate this mechanism in a fixed-magnetization sector of deterministic XXZ spin chains with a single integrability-breaking bulk defect. We derive an analytical selection rule for the Pauli kicks and show that symmetry-preserving strings with a specific domain-wall count, fixed by the couplings, govern design formation. An exhaustive search over all admissible Pauli strings identifies a broad family of kicks that produce designs in the chaotic regime, whereas no such kicks exist in the integrable limit, including for boundary defects. We further show that the design-forming mechanism remains effective for weak bulk defects as the system size increases.

title: $d$-pod Realization Of Nonadiabatic Holonomic Quantum Computation
authors: Oskar Axelsson, Claes F\"alth, Elias Henriksson Lindberg, Erik Sj\"oqvist
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Holonomic quantum computation (HQC) realizes quantum gates through non-Abelian geometric phases, providing an experimentally accessible approach to quantum control. While the nonadiabatic HQC framework has been extensively developed for three-level [MATH] systems encoding qubits, its systematic extension to higher-dimensional qudits remains largely unexplored. In this work, we generalize nonadiabatic HQC to a [MATH]-pod configuration, where a single excited state is coupled to [MATH] ground states, the latter forming the computational subspace. This scheme enables universal holonomic single- and two-qudit gates using only optical or microwave pulses on trapped atoms or ions, offering an efficient route to implement a discrete universal gate set with minimal pulse coordination. As an explicit example, we analyze in detail the qutrit ([MATH]) case, demonstrating compact realizations of single- and two-qutrit holonomic gates, each gate requiring at most two loops in the Grassmannian generated by at most three pulses.

title: Completeness Of The Fuzzy Order On Fuzzy Numbers
authors: Mingchun Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the completeness properties of the fuzzy order on the fuzzy number space [MATH] within the framework of [MATH]-enriched categories. \(S\)-convergence under the three fundamental continuous t-norms is characterized, and inclusion relations among the induced open ball topologies are established. It is shown that [MATH] is Cauchy complete if and only if the t-norm is not isomorphic to the {\L}ukasiewicz t-norm, whereas [MATH] fails to be Smyth complete for every continuous t-norm. Consequently, the symmetrization [MATH] is Smyth complete if and only if the underlying continuous t-norm is not isomorphic to the {\L}ukasiewicz t-norm.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Pressure At Infinity And Large Deviations
authors: Godofredo Iommi, Thomas Jordan, Anibal Velozo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.16220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish level-1 large deviation principles for continuous time suspension flows over countable Markov shifts, a class of non compact dynamical systems. Our results both quantify deviations of Birkhoff averages from their typical values and, importantly, provide a large deviation principle for orbits that at a finite time are close to escaping to infinity. To overcome the challenges posed by non compactness, we introduce the notion of topological pressure at infinity and prove a variational principle linking it to its measure theoretic counterpart. This framework allows the study of a natural class of potentials, known as strongly positive recurrent, which exhibit robust thermodynamic properties. Moreover, we show that compactly supported ergodic measures are pressure dense in this setting. Applications to pressure gaps and examples are given.

title: Can We Stop The Ads? Taxonomy And Characterization Of Smartphone Splash Ads And Existing Countermeasures
authors: Shuhao Zhang, Xinyu Liu, Ziyu Shao, Yuqing Yang, Yan Long
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Splash ads are full-screen advertisements that pop up and appear as the first interaction page when users start an app, often tricking users into unknowingly activating certain trigger mechanisms, such as moving the phone to redirect users to other profit-driven third parties. So far, splash ads have already caused significant real-world impacts, ranging from significantly delaying emergency response to distracting drivers, as well as degrading accessibility of apps to vision-impaired users. We analyze 108 documented implementations of advertising defenses to examine their applicability to splash ads and the requirements users face when deploying them. Our analysis identifies substantial deployment barriers, including device rooting or jailbreaking, runtime code injection, and application modification. Options without these requirements can still involve additional permissions, rule maintenance, source compilation, or payment. In our evaluation of 13 configurations of 11 tools across 10 popular apps, only one tool prevented the target ad-triggered navigation across all ten apps. It required Accessibility permission, and ads remained visible for approximately one second before dismissal. Other tested configurations failed to prevent navigation or, in some cases, left host apps unable to launch or stuck on the ad page. We further analyze the outstanding challenges and pos- sible future directions, highlighting the urgent need to incentivize smartphone manufacturers to provide more friendly and regulated platforms.
tldr: This paper taxonomizes smartphone splash ads and evaluates existing countermeasures, finding that most tools face deployment barriers and fail to prevent ad-triggered navigation.
motivation: Splash ads cause real-world harms such as delaying emergency response, distracting drivers, and reducing accessibility, prompting a need to understand and improve defenses.
method: The authors analyze 108 documented advertising defenses and evaluate 13 configurations of 11 tools across 10 popular apps to assess their applicability and deployment requirements.
result: Only one tool prevented the target ad-triggered navigation across all ten apps, requiring Accessibility permission and leaving ads visible for about one second; other configurations failed or broke host apps.
conclusion: Significant deployment barriers remain, and the authors call for incentives for smartphone manufacturers to provide more friendly and regulated platforms.
